title: Washington Hails Progress in DRC-Rwanda Peace Agreement Implementation
excerpt: Washington, D.C. - The United States welcomed what it described as a significant step forward in the implementation of the peace agreement between the Democratic Republic of Congo (DRC) and Rwanda, following high-level…
title_en: Washington Hails Progress in DRC-Rwanda Peace Agreement Implementation
excerpt_en: Washington, D.C. - The United States welcomed what it described as a significant step forward in the implementation of the peace agreement between the Democratic Republic of Congo (DRC) and Rwanda, following high-level…
body_en:
Washington, D.C. - The United States welcomed what it described as a significant step forward in the implementation of the peace agreement between the Democratic Republic of Congo (DRC) and Rwanda, following high-level talks in the U.S. capital.

Delegations from both countries convened on 21 and 22 October 2025 in Washington for the third session of the Joint Security Coordination Mechanism (JSCM). The meeting, held under the auspices of the United States, Qatar, and the African Union Commission, aimed to accelerate the execution of the peace accord signed on 27 June 2025, which had been technically initialed earlier on 18 June 2025.

Officials focused discussions on measures to neutralize the Democratic Forces for the Liberation of Rwanda (FDLR) and on the gradual lifting of Rwanda’s defensive measures, steps seen as crucial to stabilizing bilateral relations after years of tension.

“The dialogue reflects a shared commitment to peace and security in the region,” a U.S. State Department spokesperson said, emphasizing Washington’s support for continued international oversight.

The fourth session of the JSCM is already scheduled for 19 and 20 November 2025, signaling ongoing coordination between the two nations under the watchful eye of international partners. Analysts suggest that consistent engagement through the JSCM could pave the way for tangible progress in security and diplomatic cooperation along the DRC-Rwanda border.

title: DRC National Assembly: Twelve Sacred Union MPs Vie for Presidency
excerpt: Kinshasa, DRC - Twelve Members of Parliament (MPs) from the Sacred Union have officially submitted their candidacies for the presidency of the National Assembly, with no women among the contenders, coalition officials…
title_en: DRC National Assembly: Twelve Sacred Union MPs Vie for Presidency
excerpt_en: Kinshasa, DRC - Twelve Members of Parliament (MPs) from the Sacred Union have officially submitted their candidacies for the presidency of the National Assembly, with no women among the contenders, coalition officials…
body_en:
Kinshasa, DRC - Twelve Members of Parliament (MPs) from the Sacred Union have officially submitted their candidacies for the presidency of the National Assembly, with no women among the contenders, coalition officials confirmed.

The announcement came on Friday, 24 October 2025, by André Mbata, permanent secretary of the Sacred Union. The candidacy files have since been forwarded to the High Political Authority, President Félix Tshisekedi, who is the sole authority empowered to designate the official candidate to be presented for a vote in the Assembly.

Among the declared contenders are three MPs from the ruling UDPS party-Doudou Dunia Mangu Mangu, Patrick Matata Makalamba, and Crispin Mbindule Mitono-and two from the UNC, namely Aimé Boji Sangara and Jean-Baudouin Mayo Mambeke. The remaining candidates come from a range of political groups, ensuring geopolitical representation across the east, west, and center of the country.

All twelve candidates have pledged to respect the final decision of the Head of State, signaling unity behind the presidential designation process within the ruling coalition. Analysts suggest that President Tshisekedi’s choice will be pivotal in shaping the legislative agenda and political alignment in the National Assembly for the coming term.

title: Haut-Lomami Assembly President and Quaestor Dismissed Over Alleged Embezzlement
excerpt: Kamina, DRC - The President and Quaestor of the Haut-Lomami Provincial Assembly, Basile Muleba and Séraphin Mukaya, were dismissed on Friday, 24 October 2025, following a plenary session dominated by a motion of no confidence.
title_en: Haut-Lomami Assembly President and Quaestor Dismissed Over Alleged Embezzlement
excerpt_en: Kamina, DRC - The President and Quaestor of the Haut-Lomami Provincial Assembly, Basile Muleba and Séraphin Mukaya, were dismissed on Friday, 24 October 2025, following a plenary session dominated by a motion of no confidence.
body_en:
Kamina, DRC - The President and Quaestor of the Haut-Lomami Provincial Assembly, Basile Muleba and Séraphin Mukaya, were dismissed on Friday, 24 October 2025, following a plenary session dominated by a motion of no confidence. The motion was initiated by MP Jean Tayari Kiswabantu.

Of the 20 deputies present, 17 voted to remove the president and 18 voted to dismiss the quaestor, who stand accused of embezzling salaries of deputies and staff for March 2024 and May 2025, according to a memorandum submitted to the Deputy Prime Minister of the Interior.

In addition to the financial allegations, deputies criticized President Muleba for incompetence and behaviour deemed abusive and threatening, highlighting broader concerns about governance within the provincial assembly.

The session was conducted with the approval of the Ministry of the Interior, but notably, both dismissed officials were absent and did not respond to the vote. Observers suggest the decision reflects mounting pressure on provincial authorities to improve transparency and accountability.

title: Congolese Government Urges Stability Amid Crises in Provincial Assemblies
excerpt: Kinshasa, DRC - The Congolese government has voiced serious concern over rising institutional crises in several provincial assemblies, including Mai-Ndombe, Lomami, and Kwango, during the Council of Ministers meeting on…
title_en: Congolese Government Urges Stability Amid Crises in Provincial Assemblies
excerpt_en: Kinshasa, DRC - The Congolese government has voiced serious concern over rising institutional crises in several provincial assemblies, including Mai-Ndombe, Lomami, and Kwango, during the Council of Ministers meeting on…
body_en:
Kinshasa, DRC - The Congolese government has voiced serious concern over rising institutional crises in several provincial assemblies, including Mai-Ndombe, Lomami, and Kwango, during the Council of Ministers meeting on Friday, 24 October 2025.

Government spokesperson Patrick Muyaya, relaying the Council’s report, said that the Deputy Minister of the Interior outlined measures aimed at restoring order and stability in the affected institutions. The tensions, officials noted, stem from internal governance disputes and interference by some political figures attempting to exercise control over provincial administrations from Kinshasa.

To address the situation, the Ministry of the Interior plans to convene leaders of political parties to emphasize the importance of preserving institutional stability, particularly as the country continues to grapple with serious security challenges in its eastern provinces. Analysts warn that unchecked political interference could exacerbate tensions and hinder effective governance at the provincial level.

title: Eastern DRC: Government and AFC/M23 Trade Accusations Amid Ceasefire Tensions
excerpt: Goma, DRC - Tensions remain high in eastern Democratic Republic of Congo as the government and the AFC/M23 rebel movement continue to accuse each other of violating the ongoing ceasefire.
title_en: Eastern DRC: Government and AFC/M23 Trade Accusations Amid Ceasefire Tensions
excerpt_en: Goma, DRC - Tensions remain high in eastern Democratic Republic of Congo as the government and the AFC/M23 rebel movement continue to accuse each other of violating the ongoing ceasefire.
body_en:
Goma, DRC - Tensions remain high in eastern Democratic Republic of Congo as the government and the AFC/M23 rebel movement continue to accuse each other of violating the ongoing ceasefire.

On Thursday, 24 October 2025, during a press briefing in Goma, the AFC/M23 denounced attacks by the FARDC in the territories of Walikale, Masisi, and Kalehe. In response, government spokesperson Patrick Muyaya dismissed the allegations, asserting that the rebels are attempting to distract from their own abuses, which reportedly included over 270 murders, 300 rapes, and numerous cases of torture recorded in September.

The AFC/M23 has now threatened retaliation against any perceived provocation, raising fears among observers of a potential escalation of violence despite repeated calls for adherence to the ceasefire. Security analysts warn that without renewed dialogue and enforcement, the fragile truce in eastern DRC could quickly collapse.

title: DRC’s Tshisekedi in Paris Calls for Global Action to End “Protracted Tragedy” in the Great Lakes Region
excerpt: Paris, France - Democratic Republic of Congo (DRC) President Félix Antoine Tshisekedi has denounced what he called a “protracted tragedy” caused by ongoing armed aggression in eastern Congo, urging the international…
title_en: DRC’s Tshisekedi in Paris Calls for Global Action to End “Protracted Tragedy” in the Great Lakes Region
excerpt_en: Paris, France - Democratic Republic of Congo (DRC) President Félix Antoine Tshisekedi has denounced what he called a “protracted tragedy” caused by ongoing armed aggression in eastern Congo, urging the international…
body_en:
Paris, France - Democratic Republic of Congo (DRC) President Félix Antoine Tshisekedi has denounced what he called a “protracted tragedy” caused by ongoing armed aggression in eastern Congo, urging the international community to take firm and coordinated action to restore peace.

Speaking Thursday, October 30, on the sidelines of the international conference on peace and prosperity in the Great Lakes region, held in Paris, Tshisekedi accused the M23 rebel group - backed by Rwanda - of being the primary driver of the worsening humanitarian crisis in his country.

The Congolese leader called for the full implementation of UN Security Council Resolution 2773, stressing the need for stronger humanitarian coordination and sustainable funding to support millions of displaced people.

“Behind every statistic lies a human tragedy,” Tshisekedi said, insisting that true peace in the Great Lakes must rest on justice, regional economic integration, and an end to the plundering of natural resources.

He concluded by urging the world to act decisively, saying prosperity and security are inseparable in the quest for lasting stability in the region.

title: DRC-Egypt: Tshisekedi and al-Sisi Reaffirm Commitment to Strengthening Bilateral Cooperation
excerpt: Cairo, Egypt - Following his participation in the Paris conference on the humanitarian crisis in the Great Lakes region, Democratic Republic of Congo (DRC) President Félix Antoine Tshisekedi Tshilombo arrived in Cairo…
title_en: DRC-Egypt: Tshisekedi and al-Sisi Reaffirm Commitment to Strengthening Bilateral Cooperation
excerpt_en: Cairo, Egypt - Following his participation in the Paris conference on the humanitarian crisis in the Great Lakes region, Democratic Republic of Congo (DRC) President Félix Antoine Tshisekedi Tshilombo arrived in Cairo…
body_en:
Cairo, Egypt - Following his participation in the Paris conference on the humanitarian crisis in the Great Lakes region, Democratic Republic of Congo (DRC) President Félix Antoine Tshisekedi Tshilombo arrived in Cairo on Friday, October 31, 2025, responding to an official invitation from Egyptian President Abdel Fattah al-Sisi.

The Congolese president was received with full honors at Cairo International Airport, reflecting the high diplomatic significance of the visit. Soon after his arrival, Tshisekedi held a series of in-depth talks with President al-Sisi at the Al-Ittihadiya Presidential Palace, where both leaders reaffirmed their mutual commitment to strengthening bilateral relations.

Key topics on the agenda included enhancing cooperation across military, economic, and diplomatic sectors, as well as consolidating longstanding ties of friendship between the two nations. The leaders also discussed revitalizing existing partnership agreements, with an emphasis on promoting sustainable development, regional security, and economic integration within Africa.

This high-level visit is part of Kinshasa’s broader diplomatic strategy aimed at diversifying the DRC’s regional alliances and increasing its influence on the continental stage. Officials noted that the engagement with Egypt could pave the way for joint initiatives in trade, infrastructure development, and security cooperation, signaling a deepening of strategic ties between the two countries.

President Tshisekedi’s itinerary also includes bilateral meetings with Egyptian ministers and business leaders to explore investment opportunities and collaborative projects that could support the DRC’s economic growth and regional integration efforts.

The visit underscores the DRC’s proactive approach to diplomacy, positioning the country as an active player in African affairs while reinforcing its commitment to building stronger, mutually beneficial partnerships.

title: DRC: Aimé Boji Named Sacred Union’s Sole Candidate for National Assembly Presidency
excerpt: Kinshasa, DRC - National Deputy Aimé Boji Sangara, representing Walungu in South Kivu and former Minister of Industry, was officially designated on Wednesday, October 29, 2025, as the Sacred Union’s sole candidate for…
title_en: DRC: Aimé Boji Named Sacred Union’s Sole Candidate for National Assembly Presidency
excerpt_en: Kinshasa, DRC - National Deputy Aimé Boji Sangara, representing Walungu in South Kivu and former Minister of Industry, was officially designated on Wednesday, October 29, 2025, as the Sacred Union’s sole candidate for…
body_en:
Kinshasa, DRC - National Deputy Aimé Boji Sangara, representing Walungu in South Kivu and former Minister of Industry, was officially designated on Wednesday, October 29, 2025, as the Sacred Union’s sole candidate for the presidency of the National Assembly, succeeding Vital Kamerhe.

The announcement was made by André Mbata, Permanent Secretary of the Sacred Union within the presidential majority, who emphasized that Boji’s designation came through a consensus around the coalition’s moral authority, President Félix Tshisekedi.

Mbata called on Sacred Union deputies, as well as the eleven other candidates who had initially expressed interest, to rally behind Boji’s candidacy. The move aims to ensure unity and maintain stability within the parliamentary majority ahead of the election for the Assembly’s leadership.

Boji’s appointment underscores the Sacred Union’s strategy of consolidating its influence in the legislature while signaling continuity in alignment with President Tshisekedi’s political vision. Analysts note that his selection could reinforce cohesion among majority deputies and facilitate the advancement of the government’s legislative agenda.

title: Crisis in Kasai-Oriental: Governor and Provincial Assembly Bureau Summoned to Kinshasa
excerpt: Kinshasa, DRC - The escalating power struggle in Kasai-Oriental between Governor Jean-Paul Mbwebwa Kapo and the provincial assembly bureau has drawn national attention.
title_en: Crisis in Kasai-Oriental: Governor and Provincial Assembly Bureau Summoned to Kinshasa
excerpt_en: Kinshasa, DRC - The escalating power struggle in Kasai-Oriental between Governor Jean-Paul Mbwebwa Kapo and the provincial assembly bureau has drawn national attention.
body_en:
Kinshasa, DRC - The escalating power struggle in Kasai-Oriental between Governor Jean-Paul Mbwebwa Kapo and the provincial assembly bureau has drawn national attention. Following the suspension of a plenary session on Friday, October 31, convened to consider a motion of no confidence against the governor, the Ministry of the Interior issued a telegram dated October 30, summoning both parties to Kinshasa for urgent mediation.

At the center of the conflict is the contentious management of approximately $3 million allocated by the state for provincial development projects. Deputies are demanding accountability for the funds, while Governor Mbwebwa and his supporters accuse the assembly bureau of leveraging the issue for political purposes.

The situation turned volatile at the assembly headquarters in Mbuji-Mayi, where activists reportedly attempted to storm the building, overturning tables and breaking windows. The ministry’s intervention aims to de-escalate tensions and prevent a full-blown institutional crisis in the province.

Authorities in Kinshasa hope the mediation will restore dialogue and trust between the provincial government and elected representatives, ensuring that governance and oversight can proceed without further disruptions.

title: Reopening of Goma International Airport Sparks Debate Between Kigali and Kinshasa
excerpt: Goma, DRC / Paris, France - The planned reopening of Goma International Airport in North Kivu has stirred diplomatic tensions between Rwanda and the Democratic Republic of Congo (DRC).
title_en: Reopening of Goma International Airport Sparks Debate Between Kigali and Kinshasa
excerpt_en: Goma, DRC / Paris, France - The planned reopening of Goma International Airport in North Kivu has stirred diplomatic tensions between Rwanda and the Democratic Republic of Congo (DRC).
body_en:
Goma, DRC / Paris, France - The planned reopening of Goma International Airport in North Kivu has stirred diplomatic tensions between Rwanda and the Democratic Republic of Congo (DRC). The announcement was made by French President Emmanuel Macron during the Paris Peace Conference on the Great Lakes Region on October 30, 2025.

The airport, closed for nearly a year due to clashes between the FARDC (Armed Forces of the DRC) and the M23 rebel group, is being presented as a humanitarian measure aimed at improving aid access to the region. Rwanda has expressed support for the initiative, emphasizing coordination with prior Doha discussions involving the M23.

Kinshasa, however, has reacted cautiously, underlining that the airport must remain under the sole management of Congolese authorities and stressing respect for national sovereignty. Government officials warned that any unilateral actions could undermine the diplomatic progress achieved during the Paris conference.

The announcement highlights the delicate balance in the Great Lakes region, where humanitarian needs intersect with ongoing security concerns and complex regional politics. Analysts note that the airport’s reopening will require careful coordination to ensure both the delivery of aid and the preservation of DRC’s authority over its territory.

Economy and Tech.

title: DRC: President Tshisekedi Hosts Government Meeting on Congolese Franc Appreciation and Falling Prices
excerpt: Kinshasa, DRC - President Félix Antoine Tshisekedi Tshilombo convened a government meeting on Wednesday, 22 October 2025, to assess the impact of the appreciation of the Congolese franc (CDF) on the economy and…
title_en: DRC: President Tshisekedi Hosts Government Meeting on Congolese Franc Appreciation and Falling Prices
excerpt_en: Kinshasa, DRC - President Félix Antoine Tshisekedi Tshilombo convened a government meeting on Wednesday, 22 October 2025, to assess the impact of the appreciation of the Congolese franc (CDF) on the economy and…
body_en:
Kinshasa, DRC - President Félix Antoine Tshisekedi Tshilombo convened a government meeting on Wednesday, 22 October 2025, to assess the impact of the appreciation of the Congolese franc (CDF) on the economy and household purchasing power. The meeting was held at the African Union headquarters and brought together Prime Minister Judith Suminwa, key government ministers, and the Governor of the Central Bank of Congo.

According to Deputy Prime Minister in charge of the national economy, Daniel Mukoko Samba, the discussions focused on strengthening coordination between monetary and fiscal policies to ensure that the recent appreciation of the franc translates into lower market prices for goods and services.

The government is also considering a downward adjustment of petroleum product prices and plans to consult economic operators in the coming days to reinforce price controls and address public expectations. Analysts say the measures aim to stabilize the economy and protect household purchasing power amid fluctuating currency trends.

Analysts say the measures aim to stabilize the economy and protect household purchasing power amid fluctuating currency trends.

Represented by Minister of Foreign Trade Julien Paluku Kahongya, the DRC highlighted its vast opportunities in mining, agriculture, energy, infrastructure, and tourism, stressing the need for regulated multilateral trade to ensure fair exchanges between resource-rich countries and financially endowed nations.

The DRC delegation emphasized that fair trade and international cooperation are essential for leveraging the country’s resources while promoting sustainable economic growth.

Kinshasa, DRC / Luanda, Angola - The Democratic Republic of Congo and Angola are set to further strengthen their economic ties with the announcement of the 3rd DRC-Angola Economic Forum, planned for February 2026 in Muanda, Kongo-Central province.

The decision follows an official mission to Luanda by Deputy Prime Minister and Minister of National Economy Daniel Mukoko Samba from October 27 to 29, 2025. Accompanied by the High Representative of the Head of State, Tony Kanku, Mukoko Samba held meetings with key Angolan officials, including the Ministers of Planning, Industry and Trade, Fisheries and Marine Resources, and the Minister of State for Economic Coordination.

The discussions centered on boosting bilateral trade, removing obstacles to commerce, and deepening cooperation in sectors such as fishing, energy, and regional integration. Reviving partnerships with Angola’s national oil company, SONANGOL, was also a key topic.

Officials highlighted that the forum will serve as a platform to foster sustainable economic collaboration, enhance investment opportunities, and solidify the long-term economic partnership between the two neighboring countries.

title: DRC and IMF Strike Deal to Address Oil Sector Revenue Shortfalls
excerpt: Kinshasa, DRC - The Democratic Republic of Congo (DRC) and the International Monetary Fund (IMF) have reached an agreement to tackle revenue shortfalls in the country’s oil sector.
title_en: DRC and IMF Strike Deal to Address Oil Sector Revenue Shortfalls
excerpt_en: Kinshasa, DRC - The Democratic Republic of Congo (DRC) and the International Monetary Fund (IMF) have reached an agreement to tackle revenue shortfalls in the country’s oil sector.
body_en:
Kinshasa, DRC - The Democratic Republic of Congo (DRC) and the International Monetary Fund (IMF) have reached an agreement to tackle revenue shortfalls in the country’s oil sector. The accord, signed in Kinshasa on October 29, 2025, sets out the full settlement of losses recorded in 2024-which have already been cleared-as well as those for 2025, to be resolved by February 2026.

The initiative forms part of the IMF-backed economic reform program designed to enhance budget transparency, stabilize domestic oil prices, and strengthen governance across the Congolese energy sector.

Officials emphasized that the agreement is a key step toward ensuring the sector contributes effectively to national development, while improving oversight and accountability in the management of oil resources.

The Economic Situation Committee (CCE), meeting on October 28, 2025, under Prime Minister Judith Suminwa, highlighted sustained economic growth and a stable exchange rate as positive indicators.

Officials expressed confidence that these steps will contribute to a gradual stabilization of prices for goods and services, supporting overall economic resilience and the welfare of Congolese households.

title: DRC Government Intensifies Fight Against Illicit Financial Flows in Mining Sector
excerpt: Kinshasa, DRC - The Democratic Republic of Congo is stepping up efforts to combat illicit financial flows, particularly in its vital mining sector.
title_en: DRC Government Intensifies Fight Against Illicit Financial Flows in Mining Sector
excerpt_en: Kinshasa, DRC - The Democratic Republic of Congo is stepping up efforts to combat illicit financial flows, particularly in its vital mining sector.
body_en:
Kinshasa, DRC - The Democratic Republic of Congo is stepping up efforts to combat illicit financial flows, particularly in its vital mining sector. Finance Minister Doudou Fwamba announced on Wednesday, October 29, 2025, at the opening of a high-level conference on Illicit Financial Flows of Commercial Origin (IFFC) in Kinshasa, that the Suminwa government is committed to enhancing transaction traceability and tackling tax evasion.

The conference, organized by the German development agency GIZ in collaboration with the General Directorate of Taxes (DGI), the General Directorate of Customs and Excise (DGDA), and the General Directorate of Administrative, Judicial, State Property, and Equity Revenue (DGRAD), aims to develop a comprehensive roadmap for structural reform of the national tax system.

Minister Fwamba highlighted the staggering losses caused by illicit financial flows, noting they amount to billions of dollars annually, depriving the country of critical funding for education, healthcare, and infrastructure projects.

To address these challenges, the government has recently implemented a series of measures designed to improve transparency and accountability. These include the creation of CONAFASIC (National Committee for Monitoring and Analyzing Illicit Commercial Financial Flows), the adoption of international tax agreements, and the establishment of an operational unit dedicated to the exchange of tax information.

“These initiatives are essential to ensuring that mineral wealth becomes a sustainable driver of development,” Fwamba said, emphasizing that a transparent and accountable mining sector is crucial for turning the country’s natural resources into long-term economic and social benefits.

The conference brought together key stakeholders from government, industry, and international partners to discuss strategies that will strengthen fiscal governance and curb illegal practices, signaling a determined push by Kinshasa to protect the nation’s economic interests and reinforce public trust in resource management.

Kinshasa, DRC - In anticipation of the United Nations Climate Change Conference (COP 30), scheduled for 10-21 November 2025 in Belém, Brazil, the Congolese government will launch National Climate Week on Monday, 28 October 2025.

The announcement was made on Thursday, 23 October, by Minister of the Environment Marie Nyange during a joint press briefing with Minister of Communication and Media Patrick Muyaya. The initiative, backed by Prime Minister Judith Suminwa, aims to mobilize public authorities, the private sector, civil society, indigenous peoples, and local communities around strategies that will enable the DRC to defend its environmental priorities at COP 30.

Minister Nyange stressed the importance of strong state leadership and an inclusive approach to addressing the country’s climate and forestry challenges, highlighting the DRC’s commitment to sustainable development and international climate cooperation.

title_en: Beni to Open Biometric Passport Capture Centre in November
excerpt_en: Beni, DRC - The Ministry of Foreign Affairs of the Democratic Republic of Congo announced on Tuesday, 21 October 2025 the upcoming launch of a biometric passport capture centre in Beni, the provisional capital of North…
body_en:
Beni, DRC - The Ministry of Foreign Affairs of the Democratic Republic of Congo announced on Tuesday, 21 October 2025 the upcoming launch of a biometric passport capture centre in Beni, the provisional capital of North Kivu.

Scheduled to open by the end of November at the Beni town hall, the centre aims to facilitate passport issuance for residents of Beni, Butembo, and surrounding areas, reducing the need to travel to Bunia or Kinshasa.

Anselme Ponge, head of the future centre, stated that the processing time will be approximately three weeks after completion of the required formalities, which include an online application followed by payment at Equity BCDC bank. Officials say the initiative will streamline access to travel documents and improve administrative efficiency for the region’s citizens.

Kinshasa, DRC - The Ministry of National Education and New Citizenship announced on Monday, 20 October 2025, the passing of teacher Bonette Elombe, a widely admired figure in the Congolese education sector.

Renowned for her commitment and innovative teaching methods, Elombe had gained a large following on social media and was a prominent contributor to the Primary Education Quality Improvement Project (PEQIP).

The ministry paid tribute to her as a “dedicated and admired teacher”, while Prime Minister Judith Suminwa remembered her as “a passionate and creative educator who made school a place of fulfillment and joy for her students.” Colleagues and students alike mourned the loss of an educator who inspired both in and outside the classroom.

Zongo, DRC - A 600-metre bridge is set to be constructed over the Oubangui River, linking the Democratic Republic of Congo (DRC) with the Central African Republic (CAR) as part of the Douala-Mombasa road corridor.

The strategic infrastructure project, supported jointly by the two countries and backed by ECCAS and the African Development Bank, aims to facilitate cross-border trade, strengthen regional economic integration, and boost commerce.

During a site visit on 23 October 2025, Deputy Prime Minister and Minister of National Economy Daniel Mukoko Samba also inspected the central port of Zongo to evaluate trade operations. Local authorities say the bridge, together with a modern border post on the Congolese side, will ease movement for the population and serve as a catalyst for development in Zongo and the wider South Ubangi province.

title: DRC Faces Severe Cholera Outbreak: Over 1,700 Deaths and 58,000 Suspected Cases
excerpt: Kinshasa, DRC - The Ministry of Public Health of the Democratic Republic of Congo announced on Friday, 24 October 2025, that the country is experiencing one of its worst cholera epidemics in a decade, with more than…
title_en: DRC Faces Severe Cholera Outbreak: Over 1,700 Deaths and 58,000 Suspected Cases
excerpt_en: Kinshasa, DRC - The Ministry of Public Health of the Democratic Republic of Congo announced on Friday, 24 October 2025, that the country is experiencing one of its worst cholera epidemics in a decade, with more than…
body_en:
Kinshasa, DRC - The Ministry of Public Health of the Democratic Republic of Congo announced on Friday, 24 October 2025, that the country is experiencing one of its worst cholera epidemics in a decade, with more than 1,700 deaths and 58,000 suspected cases recorded since January 2025, representing a fatality rate of over 3%.

While 20 of the 26 provinces are non-endemic, the epidemic is being fueled by floods, conflicts, displacement, and inadequate water and sanitation systems. Médecins Sans Frontières (MSF), in collaboration with the Ministry of Health, has treated over 35,800 patients and vaccinated 22,000 people since January, but efforts are constrained by limited funding, insufficient staff, and coordination challenges.

Authorities and humanitarian partners are being urged to rapidly strengthen medical, logistical, and financial support to contain the outbreak, particularly ahead of the rainy season, which could worsen the crisis. Health experts warn that immediate action is crucial to prevent further loss of life.

title: DRC: Prime Minister Calls Fight Against Female Cancers a National Imperative
excerpt: Kinshasa, DRC - Speaking at the opening of a round table on women’s cancers in Kinshasa on Saturday, 25 October 2025, Prime Minister Judith Suminwa described the fight against female cancers as a “national imperative”…
title_en: DRC: Prime Minister Calls Fight Against Female Cancers a National Imperative
excerpt_en: Kinshasa, DRC - Speaking at the opening of a round table on women’s cancers in Kinshasa on Saturday, 25 October 2025, Prime Minister Judith Suminwa described the fight against female cancers as a “national imperative”…
body_en:
Kinshasa, DRC - Speaking at the opening of a round table on women’s cancers in Kinshasa on Saturday, 25 October 2025, Prime Minister Judith Suminwa described the fight against female cancers as a “national imperative”, calling for an integrated, equitable, and sustainable strategy involving the public and private sectors, development partners, and local communities.

Minister of Public Health Roger Samuel Kamba highlighted that nearly 150,000 women are diagnosed annually with breast or cervical cancer, equating to two new cases per hour, often at an advanced stage.

The government is taking steps to strengthen the national cancer control centre, decentralize screening, modernize technical facilities, and distribute anti-cancer drugs for free in six provinces. Additionally, the cervical cancer vaccine is planned for introduction in 2026.

Despite these initiatives, officials note persistent challenges, including the absence of a national cancer registry, the centralization of infrastructure in Kinshasa, and the high cost of treatment, which continue to hinder nationwide access to care.

title: DRC Pushes for Forest Valorization During Inaugural National Climate Week
excerpt: Kinshasa, DRC - The first National Climate Week in the Democratic Republic of Congo concluded on October 30, 2025, emphasizing the importance of preserving and valorizing the country’s vast forest heritage.
title_en: DRC Pushes for Forest Valorization During Inaugural National Climate Week
excerpt_en: Kinshasa, DRC - The first National Climate Week in the Democratic Republic of Congo concluded on October 30, 2025, emphasizing the importance of preserving and valorizing the country’s vast forest heritage.
body_en:
Kinshasa, DRC - The first National Climate Week in the Democratic Republic of Congo concluded on October 30, 2025, emphasizing the importance of preserving and valorizing the country’s vast forest heritage. Held over four days, the event brought together provincial ministers, civil society actors, and environmental experts to discuss strategies for sustainable forest management and climate action ahead of the COP in Belém, Brazil, scheduled for November.

Participants highlighted the potential of the government’s “Forest is Us” program as a tool for public education, climate finance mobilization, and community engagement. The forum also advocated for the creation of green jobs and called for formal recognition of Indigenous Peoples’ critical role in conserving forests and biodiversity.

Minister of the Environment, Marie Nyange, praised President Félix Tshisekedi’s commitment to sustainable development, while Prime Minister Judith Suminwa pledged to translate the forum’s recommendations into tangible policies and initiatives.

Organized around the theme “Forest, Biodiversity, and Peatlands,” the National Climate Week fostered dialogue between policymakers, experts, and local communities, aiming to strengthen the DRC’s readiness for international climate negotiations and to ensure its forest resources contribute effectively to both ecological preservation and socio-economic development.
body_fr:
Kinshasa, DRC - The first National Climate Week in the Democratic Republic of Congo concluded on October 30, 2025, emphasizing the importance of preserving and valorizing the country’s vast forest heritage. Held over four days, the event brought together provincial ministers, civil society actors, and environmental experts to discuss strategies for sustainable forest management and climate action ahead of the COP in Belém, Brazil, scheduled for November.

Participants highlighted the potential of the government’s “Forest is Us” program as a tool for public education, climate finance mobilization, and community engagement. The forum also advocated for the creation of green jobs and called for formal recognition of Indigenous Peoples’ critical role in conserving forests and biodiversity.

Minister of the Environment, Marie Nyange, praised President Félix Tshisekedi’s commitment to sustainable development, while Prime Minister Judith Suminwa pledged to translate the forum’s recommendations into tangible policies and initiatives.

Organized around the theme “Forest, Biodiversity, and Peatlands,” the National Climate Week fostered dialogue between policymakers, experts, and local communities, aiming to strengthen the DRC’s readiness for international climate negotiations and to ensure its forest resources contribute effectively to both ecological preservation and socio-economic development.

title: DRC Launches Initiative to Revitalize Agriculture in Greater Equateur
excerpt: Kinshasa, DRC - The Democratic Republic of Congo is stepping up efforts to revive agricultural production in Greater Equateur.
title_en: DRC Launches Initiative to Revitalize Agriculture in Greater Equateur
excerpt_en: Kinshasa, DRC - The Democratic Republic of Congo is stepping up efforts to revive agricultural production in Greater Equateur.
body_en:
Kinshasa, DRC - The Democratic Republic of Congo is stepping up efforts to revive agricultural production in Greater Equateur. On October 30, 2025, Deputy Prime Minister for the Economy, Daniel Mukoko Samba, and Minister of State for Agriculture and Food Security, Muhindo Nzangi, announced the creation of a joint government team dedicated to revitalizing local agricultural enterprises.

The initiative follows an eight-day field mission by Mukoko Samba to Mongala and Sud-Ubangi provinces, where he evaluated conditions at the Bwamanda Integrated Development Center. Once a cornerstone of regional agricultural production, the facility remains operational but faces decline in the cultivation of coffee, corn, cocoa, and soybeans.

The joint team is tasked with strengthening the agricultural value chain, boosting national production, and ensuring food security, aligning with President Félix Tshisekedi’s strategic priorities for the sector. Officials emphasized that a concrete action plan will be implemented with the aim of delivering visible results within the next two weeks, signaling a renewed government push to support farmers and stimulate rural economies in the region.

title: South Kivu: National Route 2 Reopens in Mwenga After Three-Week Blockade
excerpt: Mwenga, South Kivu, DRC - National Route 2 was reopened to traffic on Wednesday, October 29, 2025, after three weeks of closure in Mwenga territory, previously controlled by AFC-M23 rebels.
title_en: South Kivu: National Route 2 Reopens in Mwenga After Three-Week Blockade
excerpt_en: Mwenga, South Kivu, DRC - National Route 2 was reopened to traffic on Wednesday, October 29, 2025, after three weeks of closure in Mwenga territory, previously controlled by AFC-M23 rebels.
body_en:
Mwenga, South Kivu, DRC - National Route 2 was reopened to traffic on Wednesday, October 29, 2025, after three weeks of closure in Mwenga territory, previously controlled by AFC-M23 rebels. The reopening allows vehicles and motorcycles transporting essential goods to reach Mwenga and Kamituga, providing much-needed relief to local communities reliant on the route for food and supplies.

Despite the reopening, the road remains in a severely deteriorated condition, complicating travel and transport. Traders have reported significant losses, particularly of perishable goods that were stranded for over twenty days at the Bwahungu checkpoint. Authorities have called for urgent repairs and increased security measures to ensure safe and consistent passage along this strategic artery.

title_en: Kinshasa Hosts Economic Forum to Advance Urban and Sustainable Sanitation
excerpt_en: Kinshasa, DRC - The Kinshasa Economic Forum for Sustainable Sanitation opened on Tuesday, October 28, 2025, bringing together government officials, private sector actors, and civil society representatives for three days…
body_en:
Kinshasa, DRC - The Kinshasa Economic Forum for Sustainable Sanitation opened on Tuesday, October 28, 2025, bringing together government officials, private sector actors, and civil society representatives for three days of discussions on tackling the city’s chronic sanitation challenges.

Supported by the Embassy of the Netherlands, the forum aimed to foster partnerships in waste management and promote shared civic responsibility. Key speakers, including Dutch Deputy Ambassador Jennyfer Imperator and City of Kinshasa representative Melia Bosiki, emphasized the importance of changing public mindset and mobilizing collective action to improve urban hygiene.

The city has already taken concrete steps, reopening the Mpasa landfill and receiving 100 of the 300 trucks planned to enhance waste collection and management. Organizers stressed that collaborative efforts between authorities, communities, and international partners are essential to ensuring sustainable sanitation solutions for Kinshasa’s growing population.

title: Ituri: UNICEF Provides Humanitarian Aid to Over 3,700 Displaced and Returnee Families in Tchomia
excerpt: Tchomia, Ituri, DRC - The United Nations Children’s Fund (UNICEF), in partnership with the Primary Health Care Prevention Program (PPSSP), has distributed essential humanitarian assistance to 3,716 displaced and…
title_en: Ituri: UNICEF Provides Humanitarian Aid to Over 3,700 Displaced and Returnee Families in Tchomia
excerpt_en: Tchomia, Ituri, DRC - The United Nations Children’s Fund (UNICEF), in partnership with the Primary Health Care Prevention Program (PPSSP), has distributed essential humanitarian assistance to 3,716 displaced and…
body_en:
Tchomia, Ituri, DRC - The United Nations Children’s Fund (UNICEF), in partnership with the Primary Health Care Prevention Program (PPSSP), has distributed essential humanitarian assistance to 3,716 displaced and returnee families in the Tchomia chiefdom, Ituri province.

The aid, funded by the USAID Office of Humanitarian Assistance (BHA) under the Unirr project, includes blankets, cooking utensils, lightweight shelter kits, and feminine hygiene products, aimed at improving living conditions for families affected by recent clashes between local militias and the Congolese armed forces.

Beneficiaries include individuals returning from Uganda as well as internally displaced households, many of whom live in extreme poverty compounded by inadequate shelter and the limited capacity of host families. UNICEF emphasized that the support is part of ongoing efforts to provide urgent relief and protect vulnerable populations in conflict-affected areas of eastern DRC.

title_en: Kinshasa: Activists Launch “Front for the Fourth Republic” to Drive Citizen-Led Constitutional Reform
excerpt_en: Kinshasa, DRC - On Monday, October 27, 2025, Congolese activists launched the “Front for the Fourth Republic” in Kinshasa, a citizen-driven initiative aimed at promoting constitutional reform tailored to the country’s…
body_en:
Kinshasa, DRC - On Monday, October 27, 2025, Congolese activists launched the “Front for the Fourth Republic” in Kinshasa, a citizen-driven initiative aimed at promoting constitutional reform tailored to the country’s cultural and social realities.

Dady Tshisuaka, one of the movement’s founders, explained that the initiative seeks to collect over one million signatures in line with Article 218 of the Constitution, with the goal of proposing a revision that would transition the nation from the Third to the Fourth Republic.

Described by its organizers as a non-political effort, the movement emphasizes returning power to the people and establishing citizen oversight mechanisms to foster sustainable development and strengthen good governance. The initiative signals growing civic engagement in shaping the country’s political and institutional future.

excerpt_en: Kinzau Nvuete, Kongo-Central, DRC - On Saturday, October 25, 2025, Governor Grâce Nkuanga Bilolo officially launched the rehabilitation of 550 kilometers of agricultural access roads in the Seke-Banza territory.
body_en:
Kinzau Nvuete, Kongo-Central, DRC - On Saturday, October 25, 2025, Governor Grâce Nkuanga Bilolo officially launched the rehabilitation of 550 kilometers of agricultural access roads in the Seke-Banza territory.

Funded with 3.85 billion Congolese francs by the Toll and Weighing Rights Management Agency (AGDP), the project aims to open up rural areas, improve transportation of agricultural products, and stimulate local economic activity.

Implemented by the Kongo-Central Public Works Agency, the first phase-scheduled over nine months-will focus on key axes including Kinzau-Mvuete, Seke-Banza, Mbatassiala, and Lombo-Fuese-Kilukweta. Authorities highlighted that the upgraded roads will better connect production basins to urban markets, enhancing food security and fostering sustainable development across the province.

title_en: Kinshasa: Trial Opens for Honorine Porsche and Accomplices Over Failed Rawbank Heist
excerpt_en: Kinshasa, DRC - The military court of Kinshasa/Gombe opened the trial on Friday, October 24, 2025, for Honorine Porsche, a Congolese woman of German origin, and four co-defendants, following the failed robbery of the…
body_en:
Kinshasa, DRC - The military court of Kinshasa/Gombe opened the trial on Friday, October 24, 2025, for Honorine Porsche, a Congolese woman of German origin, and four co-defendants, following the failed robbery of the Rawbank branch at Place Victoire on October 16.

Porsche, identified as the gang leader, faces charges of terrorism, armed robbery, and criminal conspiracy, while her accomplices are charged with armed robbery and criminal conspiracy. Rawbank has filed a civil suit, reporting losses of $10,500 during the attempted heist.

After the defendants were formally identified, the court adjourned proceedings until October 28 to allow legal counsel access to the case files. The public hearing, closely followed by Kinshasa residents, comes amid heightened efforts to combat organized crime. Meanwhile, separate proceedings are underway against law enforcement officers accused of abuses during the arrest of the suspects.

title_en: Kinshasa Journalists Join “Kinshasa Ezo Bonga” Campaign for a Cleaner City
excerpt_en: Kinshasa, DRC - Around 100 journalists from the National Union of the Congolese Press (UNPC) took part in the “Kinshasa ezo bonga” programme on Saturday, 25 October 2025, demonstrating their commitment to a cleaner and…
body_en:
Kinshasa, DRC - Around 100 journalists from the National Union of the Congolese Press (UNPC) took part in the “Kinshasa ezo bonga” programme on Saturday, 25 October 2025, demonstrating their commitment to a cleaner and healthier city.

The initiative, launched by Governor Daniel Bumba, saw journalists gather at Place des Evolués in Gombe, equipped with shovels, rakes, and brooms, to clean this key crossroads in the capital.

Jean Marie Kassamba, president of UNPC/Kinshasa, emphasized that the action is meant to support city council efforts and set a positive example beyond the usual role of critique. Rachel Kitsita, UNPC treasurer, welcomed the initiative, urging the press to remain civic-minded and socially responsible.

Kassamba announced that the operation will rotate every two weeks across various municipalities-including Lingwala, Bandalungwa, Kisenso, Limete, Maluku, Kalamu, Bumbu, and Makala-to amplify the impact of the programme and foster greater citizen engagement in urban cleanliness.

title_en: Paris: Congolese Civil Society Advocates for Special Tribunal to Support Peace and Justice in DRC
excerpt_en: Paris, France - On October 30, 2025, during the International Conference in Support of Peace and Prosperity in the Great Lakes Region, Nene Bintu, president of the South Kivu Civil Society Coordination Office, called…
body_en:
Paris, France - On October 30, 2025, during the International Conference in Support of Peace and Prosperity in the Great Lakes Region, Nene Bintu, president of the South Kivu Civil Society Coordination Office, called for the creation of a special tribunal for the Democratic Republic of Congo.

Bintu emphasized that such a tribunal, complementing the International Criminal Court, is vital to ensuring lasting peace and delivering justice to victims of armed conflict, particularly women and youth who are often marginalized in peace processes.

She further highlighted the importance of pairing humanitarian assistance with civilian protection and actively promoting the inclusion of women in peacebuilding and mediation efforts. Bintu’s appeal aligns with the principles of feminist diplomacy championed by Nobel Peace Prize laureate Denis Mukwege, underscoring the role of inclusive approaches in achieving sustainable peace in the region.

title: DRC: Consular Judges Strike Over Unpaid Salaries, Threatening Commercial Justice
excerpt: Kinshasa, DRC - Consular judges in the Democratic Republic of Congo have extended their strike, protesting the non-payment of salaries since the creation of commercial courts.
title_en: DRC: Consular Judges Strike Over Unpaid Salaries, Threatening Commercial Justice
excerpt_en: Kinshasa, DRC - Consular judges in the Democratic Republic of Congo have extended their strike, protesting the non-payment of salaries since the creation of commercial courts.
body_en:
Kinshasa, DRC - Consular judges in the Democratic Republic of Congo have extended their strike, protesting the non-payment of salaries since the creation of commercial courts. The issue was raised during a meeting on Monday, October 27, 2025, with Justice Minister Guillaume Ngefa.

The judges stressed that the 2023 law mandating payment of their salaries by the Public Treasury has yet to be implemented, a situation that is partially paralyzing the country’s commercial justice system.

Minister Ngefa assured that he would consult with the Ministries of Budget and Finance and the Prime Minister’s Office to address the issue. Meanwhile, consular judges, who play a critical role in resolving economic disputes, are calling for an urgent solution to safeguard the dignity of their office and ensure the proper functioning of the courts.

title: Lisbon: Congolese Human Rights Minister Calls for Recognition of Genocide at Council of Europe

title_en: Lisbon: Congolese Human Rights Minister Calls for Recognition of Genocide at Council of Europe
excerpt_en: Lisbon, Portugal - On the sidelines of the Council of Europe conference opening Wednesday, October 29, 2025, Congolese Minister of Human Rights Samuel Mbemba called for international recognition of the Congolese…
body_en:
Lisbon, Portugal - On the sidelines of the Council of Europe conference opening Wednesday, October 29, 2025, Congolese Minister of Human Rights Samuel Mbemba called for international recognition of the Congolese genocide and an end to global silence regarding Rwandan aggression, which he said has claimed over 10 million lives.

Mbemba urged member states to strongly condemn the aggression, warning that inaction would amount to complicity. In response, members of the Executive Committee observed a moment of silence in memory of the victims in eastern DRC.

The minister also highlighted achievements of the Suminwa government in human rights, citing progress in judicial reforms, anti-corruption measures, gender equality initiatives, free education, and universal health coverage, underscoring ongoing efforts to strengthen governance and protect citizens’ rights.

title: Ituri: Police Officer Killed and Residents Missing After ADF Attack in Kamagolo
excerpt: Kamagolo, Ituri, DRC - A suspected ADF rebel attack on the night of 23-24 October 2025 left one police officer dead, a lorry burned, and several residents missing in the village of Kamagolo, located 45 kilometres from…
title_en: Ituri: Police Officer Killed and Residents Missing After ADF Attack in Kamagolo
excerpt_en: Kamagolo, Ituri, DRC - A suspected ADF rebel attack on the night of 23-24 October 2025 left one police officer dead, a lorry burned, and several residents missing in the village of Kamagolo, located 45 kilometres from…
body_en:
Kamagolo, Ituri, DRC - A suspected ADF rebel attack on the night of 23-24 October 2025 left one police officer dead, a lorry burned, and several residents missing in the village of Kamagolo, located 45 kilometres from Komanda in the Irumu territory of Ituri.

Local sources reported that the attackers, fleeing military operations near Lolwa on the Komanda-Mambasa axis, retreated into the nearby forest before launching the assault. The incident, occurring in an area previously considered peaceful, has prompted a mass exodus of villagers to the Mukasila 1 and 2 sites.

title_en: South Kivu: Two New Commanders Take Office in 33rd Military Region
excerpt_en: Uvira, South Kivu, DRC - On Wednesday, 22 October 2025, Brigadier General Jean-Jacques Ilunga Kabamba assumed command of the 33rd military region in Uvira, while General Amuli Civiri was appointed commander of the…
body_en:
Uvira, South Kivu, DRC - On Wednesday, 22 October 2025, Brigadier General Jean-Jacques Ilunga Kabamba assumed command of the 33rd military region in Uvira, while General Amuli Civiri was appointed commander of the Sokola 2 operational sector in South Kivu.

The officers arrived through the Kavimvira gate on the Burundi border, succeeding General Mwehu Lumbu Evariste and following the death of General Mwaku Mbuluku Jean-Daniel in August. Their appointments come amid a tense security environment, including the occupation of Bukavu by the AFC-M23 movement in February 2025 and violent protests linked to prior military postings.

The installation of these experienced commanders aims to strengthen military operations and stabilize the region, with their official inauguration attended by members of the general staff of the 33rd military region and the Sokola 2 sector. Analysts say the appointments signal a renewed focus on security and operational efficiency in this strategic area.

body_en:
Ihula, North Kivu, DRC - On Thursday, 23 October 2025, heavy fighting erupted between the Armed Forces of the DRC (FARDC), supported by Wazalendo self-defense groups, and AFC/M23 rebels in the town of Ihula, Walikale territory, prompting widespread panic and mass displacement of residents to safer areas.

Gunfire from heavy and light weapons was reported from 4 a.m. in several villages near Kalembe, including Katobi, Kalonge, and Matenge. The clashes follow FARDC airstrikes conducted the previous day in Kashebere, along with similar operations in Ihula and Nyarushyamba in the Osso-Banyungu sector.

The violence underscores the continuing volatility in North Kivu and highlights the urgent need for humanitarian assistance to protect civilians and prevent further escalation of the conflict.

title_en: South Kivu: Clashes Between AFC-M23 and Wazalendo Paralyse Nyangezi
excerpt_en: Nyangezi, South Kivu, DRC - Violent clashes between AFC-M23 rebels and Wazalendo self-defense groups on 21-22 October 2025 have plunged the Nyangezi region of Walungu territory into a severe security crisis.
body_en:
Nyangezi, South Kivu, DRC - Violent clashes between AFC-M23 rebels and Wazalendo self-defense groups on 21-22 October 2025 have plunged the Nyangezi region of Walungu territory into a severe security crisis.

The localities of Irhaga, Bwenda, Chiyanja, and Businga were hit by heavy gunfire from both heavy and light weapons, forcing the partial closure of schools, including the Weza School Complex, and halting economic activity in the area.

Thousands of residents fled to Bukavu, while the Nyangezi-Kamanyola road remains closed, hampering humanitarian aid deliveries. The clashes follow earlier attacks by AFC-M23 on Wazalendo positions in Mazigiro, Kamisimbi, underscoring the urgent need for intervention by authorities and humanitarian organizations to protect civilians and stabilize the region.

title_en: Masisi: Recurring Clashes Between AFC-M23 and Wazalendo Heighten Insecurity
excerpt_en: Masisi, North Kivu, DRC - Intense fighting erupted on Tuesday, 21 October 2025, between AFC-M23 rebels and Wazalendo fighters affiliated with Jean-Marie Bonane’s Alliance of Congolese Nationalists for the Defence of…
body_en:
Masisi, North Kivu, DRC - Intense fighting erupted on Tuesday, 21 October 2025, between AFC-M23 rebels and Wazalendo fighters affiliated with Jean-Marie Bonane’s Alliance of Congolese Nationalists for the Defence of Human Rights (ANCDH) in the Bashali Mokoto group, Masisi territory. Villages affected include Kinyana, Bibwe, and Nyabiondo.

The clashes, occurring between 5 and 8 a.m., involved heavy and light weapons, prompting civilians to flee to Bulende, Kasopo, and Lukweti, and severely disrupting local socio-economic activities.

Despite repeated calls for a ceasefire, violence has persisted for over a month in western Masisi and southwestern Rutshuru. The previous day, a Wazalendo attack in Nyabiondo left one child dead and four wounded, highlighting the ongoing fragility of security in the region.

excerpt: Miala, Ituri, DRC - On Friday, 24 October 2025, 311 ex-combatants and community members were socio-economically reintegrated in Miala, near Bunia, under the Disarmament, Demobilisation and Reintegration (DDR) programme…
title_en: Ituri: 311 Ex-Combatants Reintegrated in Miala to Strengthen Local Peace
excerpt_en: Miala, Ituri, DRC - On Friday, 24 October 2025, 311 ex-combatants and community members were socio-economically reintegrated in Miala, near Bunia, under the Disarmament, Demobilisation and Reintegration (DDR) programme…
body_en:
Miala, Ituri, DRC - On Friday, 24 October 2025, 311 ex-combatants and community members were socio-economically reintegrated in Miala, near Bunia, under the Disarmament, Demobilisation and Reintegration (DDR) programme supported by MONUSCO and implemented by the NGO Peace Mwangaza.

The participants received agricultural tools, including spades, pickaxes, and seeds, enabling them to engage in collective activities aimed at financial autonomy and community cohesion. They are also involved in the rehabilitation of agricultural access roads while awaiting their first harvests.

The initiative, which encompasses over 900 people in Telega, Tsere, Tchomia, and Miala, provides a sustainable alternative to armed violence and encourages active militiamen to join the peace process, reinforcing stability in the Ituri region.

Kinshasa, DRC - On Friday, 24 October 2025, President Félix Tshisekedi established a permanent task force to evaluate and strengthen the Democratic Republic of Congo’s efforts in combating sexual violence linked to armed conflict.

Coordinated by the presidential coordinator in charge of youth, combating violence against women, and human trafficking, the task force will regularly convene representatives from relevant institutions to monitor and enhance government action in this critical area.

Kalemie, Tanganyika, DRC - On 16 October 2025, the United Nations Children’s Fund (UNICEF) delivered non-food assistance to 3,544 displaced families residing at the Gare-Makala site, approximately 30 kilometres from Kalemie.

The aid, distributed by the DRC Red Cross under the Rapid Response (UniRR) project funded by BHA and ECHO, included kitchen utensils, mats, soap, and sanitary towels for women and girls. This support, part of the Water, Sanitation, and Hygiene (WASH) component, aims to improve conditions for over 15,000 people displaced by armed violence in North Kivu, South Kivu, and Tanganyika.

Beneficiaries expressed gratitude to UNICEF, noting that the assistance brings hope to victims of conflict and helps alleviate the hardships of displacement.

Mbandaka, Equateur, DRC - On Friday, 24 October 2025, the province of Equateur celebrated the 80th anniversary of the United Nations in a ceremony attended by local authorities, UN agency representatives, and civil society actors.

During the event, the deputy governor issued an urgent appeal for UN agencies to maintain their offices in the region, warning that the planned closure of UNICEF’s local office by the end of November 2025 could undermine programs designed to protect and support vulnerable children.

Participants highlighted the historic partnership between the UN and Equateur province, emphasizing the need for continued collaboration to advance local development and social programs.

excerpt_en: Tanganyika, DRC - The province of Tanganyika is witnessing a heightened humanitarian response by UNICEF, which announced on 25 October 2025 that it would expand interventions for people displaced by military operations…

Tanganyika, DRC - The province of Tanganyika is witnessing a heightened humanitarian response by UNICEF, which announced on 25 October 2025 that it would expand interventions for people displaced by military operations and community violence.

At the Kinyema and Mangala sites, where thousands of Bantu and Twa communities have sought refuge since January 2025, UNICEF has distributed household kits, hygiene items, and provided free healthcare for vulnerable populations. The organisation has also assisted 3,544 families at the Gare-Makala site near Kalemie with mats, blankets, and other non-food items, while establishing a reception and training centre for unaccompanied children and survivors of sexual violence.

These measures aim to address critical challenges, including limited access to clean water, malnutrition, and school dropout, amid a serious humanitarian crisis in the province.

title_en: North Kivu: At Least 12 Civilians Killed in Series of ADF Attacks in Lubero Territory
excerpt_en: Lubero, North Kivu, DRC - A series of attacks attributed to Ugandan Allied Democratic Forces (ADF) rebels left at least twelve civilians dead and several homes burned between Tuesday and Thursday, October 30, in the…
body_en:
Lubero, North Kivu, DRC - A series of attacks attributed to Ugandan Allied Democratic Forces (ADF) rebels left at least twelve civilians dead and several homes burned between Tuesday and Thursday, October 30, in the towns of Mulunguma, Gbado, and Pangoyi, over 100 kilometers from Lubero town.

According to Lubero territory administrator Colonel Alain Kiwewa, the assailants looted a local clinic and pharmacy, abducted several civilians, and stole livestock. A rapid intervention by joint FARDC-UPDF forces freed the hostages and recovered the stolen animals.

The attacks, which claimed six lives in Gbado, four in Mulunguma, and two in Pangoyi, underscore the ongoing insecurity in eastern DRC despite the presence of coalition forces. Authorities continue to call for heightened vigilance and stronger security measures to protect vulnerable communities in the region.

title: Great Lakes: Germany and Belgium Pledge Over €80 Million to Address Humanitarian Crisis
excerpt: Paris, France - At the international conference on the Great Lakes region held Thursday, October 30, 2025, Germany and Belgium announced combined financial support exceeding €80 million to respond to the ongoing…
title_en: Great Lakes: Germany and Belgium Pledge Over €80 Million to Address Humanitarian Crisis
excerpt_en: Paris, France - At the international conference on the Great Lakes region held Thursday, October 30, 2025, Germany and Belgium announced combined financial support exceeding €80 million to respond to the ongoing…
body_en:
Paris, France - At the international conference on the Great Lakes region held Thursday, October 30, 2025, Germany and Belgium announced combined financial support exceeding €80 million to respond to the ongoing humanitarian crisis, particularly in the Democratic Republic of Congo.

Germany committed €53.5 million over three years (2025-2027), while Belgium pledged €26.6 million for 2025 and €24.6 million for 2026. The funds are earmarked to improve access to humanitarian aid, protect civilians, and strengthen the resilience of local communities affected by conflict and insecurity.

Officials emphasized that these contributions reflect a shared commitment to promoting peace, stability, and sustainable development in a region grappling with complex security and humanitarian challenges.

Organizers stressed that the mobilization represents a strong international commitment to supporting stability and humanitarian relief in one of the world’s most conflict-affected areas.

title: UN Secretary-General Guterres Highlights Severe Humanitarian Crisis in the DRC
excerpt: Paris, France - At the Great Lakes Peace Conference on October 30, 2025, UN Secretary-General António Guterres sounded the alarm over the humanitarian situation in the Democratic Republic of Congo, describing it as one…
title_en: UN Secretary-General Guterres Highlights Severe Humanitarian Crisis in the DRC
excerpt_en: Paris, France - At the Great Lakes Peace Conference on October 30, 2025, UN Secretary-General António Guterres sounded the alarm over the humanitarian situation in the Democratic Republic of Congo, describing it as one…
body_en:
Paris, France - At the Great Lakes Peace Conference on October 30, 2025, UN Secretary-General António Guterres sounded the alarm over the humanitarian situation in the Democratic Republic of Congo, describing it as one of the most severe globally.

Guterres reported that over 21 million Congolese require assistance, 5.7 million are displaced, and more than 27 million are experiencing food insecurity. He also warned that essential services are collapsing amid ongoing violence in North Kivu, South Kivu, and Ituri.

While acknowledging recent diplomatic progress, including agreements brokered by the United States and Qatar, Guterres called on the international community to increase funding for the Humanitarian Response Plan and to support the immediate implementation of peace agreements, stressing the urgency of restoring stability and dignity to the Congolese people.

title: DRC: Over 32,000 Children Remain in Armed Groups in Eastern Provinces
excerpt: Beni, DRC - The Regional Network of Civil Society Organizations Against the Recruitment and Use of Child Soldiers reported on October 29 that more than 32,000 children are still active in armed groups across Ituri…
title_en: DRC: Over 32,000 Children Remain in Armed Groups in Eastern Provinces
excerpt_en: Beni, DRC - The Regional Network of Civil Society Organizations Against the Recruitment and Use of Child Soldiers reported on October 29 that more than 32,000 children are still active in armed groups across Ituri…
body_en:
Beni, DRC - The Regional Network of Civil Society Organizations Against the Recruitment and Use of Child Soldiers reported on October 29 that more than 32,000 children are still active in armed groups across Ituri, Maniema, Tanganyika, North Kivu, and South Kivu.

Speaking at the conclusion of a child protection workshop in Beni, participants urged the Congolese government to restore state authority in these conflict-affected areas and prioritize the separation and reintegration of child soldiers into their communities.

The network also called on the international community to strengthen support for ongoing peace processes, stressing that persistent insecurity continues to drive the recruitment of minors. Experts noted that without coordinated efforts, children remain highly vulnerable to exploitation, trauma, and disrupted education, underscoring the urgent need for comprehensive protection and rehabilitation programs.

title: North Kivu: Nearly 9,000 New Displaced Households Registered in Kibirizi Health Zone
excerpt: Kibirizi, North Kivu, DRC - Humanitarian authorities reported on October 29 that approximately 44,000 people, representing nearly 9,000 displaced households, have been registered in the Kibirizi health zone between late…
title_en: North Kivu: Nearly 9,000 New Displaced Households Registered in Kibirizi Health Zone
excerpt_en: Kibirizi, North Kivu, DRC - Humanitarian authorities reported on October 29 that approximately 44,000 people, representing nearly 9,000 displaced households, have been registered in the Kibirizi health zone between late…
body_en:
Kibirizi, North Kivu, DRC - Humanitarian authorities reported on October 29 that approximately 44,000 people, representing nearly 9,000 displaced households, have been registered in the Kibirizi health zone between late September and late October.

The majority of the new arrivals come from the Ikobo and Kisimba communities in Walikale territory, fleeing violent clashes between the AFC-M23 armed coalition and Wazalendo groups. Displaced families arrived in two successive waves along the Kyahala-Mirangi-Lusogha axis, reporting urgent needs for food, household supplies, and financial support.

These households join over 7,000 others already settled in the region since July, many of whom recently received assistance from the NGO Mercy Corps. Humanitarian organizations are calling for continued support to address the growing needs of displaced populations in North Kivu.

excerpt_en: Beni, North Kivu, DRC - During a visit to Beni on October 30, Evelyn Etti, Deputy Director of the World Food Programme (WFP) in the DRC, reaffirmed the organization’s commitment to providing humanitarian assistance to…
body_en:
Beni, North Kivu, DRC - During a visit to Beni on October 30, Evelyn Etti, Deputy Director of the World Food Programme (WFP) in the DRC, reaffirmed the organization’s commitment to providing humanitarian assistance to displaced populations in North Kivu, despite ongoing financial constraints.

Following discussions with the provincial vice-governor, Etti announced an upcoming WFP mission to Walikale to assess local needs on the ground. She thanked provincial authorities for their support and emphasized that the nutrition of women and children remains a top priority.

Etti stressed that the WFP will continue to support displaced families in the region for as long as necessary, highlighting the organization’s ongoing role in mitigating the humanitarian impact of conflict in eastern DRC.

title: Ituri: FARDC Seizes Weapons Cache from CRP Militia in Djugu
excerpt: Djugu, Ituri, DRC - The Armed Forces of the Democratic Republic of Congo (FARDC) recovered a significant cache of weapons and ammunition from the Convention for the Popular Revolution (CRP) militia, led by Thomas…
title_en: Ituri: FARDC Seizes Weapons Cache from CRP Militia in Djugu
excerpt_en: Djugu, Ituri, DRC - The Armed Forces of the Democratic Republic of Congo (FARDC) recovered a significant cache of weapons and ammunition from the Convention for the Popular Revolution (CRP) militia, led by Thomas…
body_en:
Djugu, Ituri, DRC - The Armed Forces of the Democratic Republic of Congo (FARDC) recovered a significant cache of weapons and ammunition from the Convention for the Popular Revolution (CRP) militia, led by Thomas Lubanga, in Djugu on Wednesday, October 29.

The seized arsenal included eight AK-47 assault rifles, two AK-56 rifles, an Uzi submachine gun, and assorted ammunition, reportedly hidden by the militia following its defeat in military operations last Sunday.

Army spokesperson Lieutenant Jules Ngongo stated that the operations are part of ongoing efforts to pacify the region and restore state authority. Military Governor Lieutenant General Johnny Luboya N’kashama praised the FARDC for their professionalism and reiterated that operations will continue to eliminate all forms of violence in this part of Ituri.

Overall Conclusion: DRC Report, October 20-31, 2025

The period between October 20 and 31, 2025, for the Democratic Republic of Congo (DRC) was characterized by a delicate balance between intensified diplomatic and economic engagement and persistent, severe security and humanitarian crises, particularly in the eastern provinces.

On the political and diplomatic fronts, the DRC made notable strides in regional and international relations:

DRC-Rwanda Peace: The United States welcomed significant progress in implementing the peace agreement, following the third session of the Joint Security Coordination Mechanism (JSCM) in Washington, which focused on neutralizing the FDLR and lifting Rwanda’s defensive measures.

National Assembly Leadership: The ruling Sacred Union, under President Félix Tshisekedi's authority, designated Aimé Boji Sangara as its sole candidate for the National Assembly presidency, aiming to consolidate political unity.

International Diplomacy: President Tshisekedi engaged in high-level diplomacy in Paris, urging global action to end the "protracted tragedy" in the Great Lakes region and securing a €1.5 billion pledge for peace and humanitarian aid. He also strengthened bilateral cooperation with Egypt in military, economic, and diplomatic sectors.

Efforts were focused on internal economic reform and external trade:

Currency and Prices: The government held a meeting to assess the appreciation of the Congolese franc (CDF), aiming to translate currency gains into lower market prices and launching a national campaign to combat price speculation.

Oil Sector Reform: The DRC and the IMF reached an agreement to resolve revenue shortfalls in the oil sector as part of a broader reform program to enhance budget transparency.

Regional Economic Ties: The 3rd DRC-Angola Economic Forum was scheduled for February 2026 to boost bilateral trade and cooperation. The construction of a 600-meter bridge linking Zongo to Bangui (CAR) was highlighted as a key infrastructure project for regional integration.

Despite diplomatic efforts, the security situation remains highly volatile, driving a catastrophic humanitarian crisis:

Escalating Violence: Intense clashes between the FARDC/Wazalendo and the AFC/M23 rebels were reported in North Kivu (Masisi, Walikale) and South Kivu (Nyangezi), prompting mass displacement and the U.S. to warn against ceasefire violations. The DRC government and the AFC/M23 continued to trade accusations over truce breaches.

ADF Attacks: Attacks attributed to the ADF rebels continued in Ituri (Kamagolo) and North Kivu (Lubero), resulting in civilian deaths, abductions, and mass displacement.

Humanitarian Scale: UN Secretary-General Guterres described the situation as one of the most severe globally, noting over 21 million people require assistance, 5.7 million are displaced, and 32,000 children remain in armed groups.

Health Crises: The country faced one of its worst cholera epidemics in a decade, with over 1,700 deaths and 58,000 suspected cases recorded since January 2025. The Prime Minister also declared the fight against female cancers a "national imperative".

In summary, the end of October 2025 demonstrated the DRC's determined push for a political solution to its conflicts and economic stability, notably through the JSCM and currency management. However, these positive steps are continuously undermined by rampant insecurity, inter-militia clashes, and the resulting, massive humanitarian and public health emergencies in the east.
