title: Rwanda Embraces 5G: A Glimpse Into the Future of Smart Technology
excerpt: Five months after the official launch of 5G high-speed internet in Rwanda, the country is beginning to witness the potential of this transformative technology across various sectors.
title_en: Rwanda Embraces 5G: A Glimpse Into the Future of Smart Technology
excerpt_en: Five months after the official launch of 5G high-speed internet in Rwanda, the country is beginning to witness the potential of this transformative technology across various sectors.
body_en:
Five months after the official launch of 5G high-speed internet in Rwanda, the country is beginning to witness the potential of this transformative technology across various sectors. The milestone was first achieved by MTN Rwanda, which introduced the service at Kigali Heights and the Kigali Convention Centre (KCC)-marking Rwanda’s entry into the era of ultra-fast connectivity.

5G technology offers lightning-fast data transfer speeds-up to 1.0 gigabit per second (Gbps)-making it 10 to 100 times faster than current internet services, including fiber optic networks. This capability opens up opportunities for innovations such as remote surgery, self-driving vehicles, industrial automation, real-time gaming, and robotics.

The service, powered by Ericsson, connects multiple devices within a radius of about one kilometer, supporting a vast network of sensors, cameras, and smart machines that can communicate and operate seamlessly. Ericsson, which also partners with Airtel Rwanda, showcased the potential of 5G during the Mobile World Congress (MWC) held in Kigali, where it demonstrated how ultra-fast internet can transform industries and daily life.

One of the standout exhibits was a robotic dog, equipped with a camera, four flexible legs, and a 5G-enabled router using MTN’s SIM card. The robot was designed to perform industrial safety and monitoring tasks, including detecting fires, identifying broken fences, and ensuring workers wear proper safety gear.

“This robot helps ensure that employees are properly dressed for work. We no longer need someone walking around to monitor everything,” said Espoir Ndayishimiye, an Ericsson Rwanda engineer. “Artificial Intelligence and 5G allow it to operate continuously and respond instantly without delay.”

The robot communicates alerts through three methods-sending text messages, app notifications, or audible alarms-making it a useful tool for industries seeking efficiency and round-the-clock surveillance.

In addition to robotics, Ericsson showcased other 5G-powered innovations, such as multiplayer gaming platforms that connect users from different countries in real time, and the Ray-Ban Meta AI Smart Glasses, which integrate augmented reality (AR) and artificial intelligence (AI). These smart glasses can take photos and videos, play music, describe surroundings, report temperature, and even tell time-all through voice commands.

Globally, 5G technology is expected to be a major economic driver, projected to generate $13.2 trillion in revenue and create 22 million new jobs by 2035. So far, 5G networks have been deployed in 101 countries, including 15 across Africa.

With 5G already reaching over five million people in Rwanda, experts believe the technology will accelerate the nation’s transition toward a digital economy, fueling innovation in health care, manufacturing, education, and smart city development.

As Rwanda continues to expand 5G coverage, it positions itself among Africa’s leading digital pioneers-embracing the next wave of technological transformation that promises to reshape industries and everyday life.

“This robot helps ensure that employees are properly dressed for work. We no longer need someone walking around to monitor everything,” said Espoir Ndayishimiye, an Ericsson Rwanda engineer. “Artificial Intelligence and 5G allow it to operate continuously and respond instantly without delay.”

The robot communicates alerts through three methods-sending text messages, app notifications, or audible alarms-making it a useful tool for industries seeking efficiency and round-the-clock surveillance.

In addition to robotics, Ericsson showcased other 5G-powered innovations, such as multiplayer gaming platforms that connect users from different countries in real time, and the Ray-Ban Meta AI Smart Glasses, which integrate augmented reality (AR) and artificial intelligence (AI). These smart glasses can take photos and videos, play music, describe surroundings, report temperature, and even tell time-all through voice commands.

Globally, 5G technology is expected to be a major economic driver, projected to generate $13.2 trillion in revenue and create 22 million new jobs by 2035. So far, 5G networks have been deployed in 101 countries, including 15 across Africa.

With 5G already reaching over five million people in Rwanda, experts believe the technology will accelerate the nation’s transition toward a digital economy, fueling innovation in health care, manufacturing, education, and smart city development.

As Rwanda continues to expand 5G coverage, it positions itself among Africa’s leading digital pioneers-embracing the next wave of technological transformation that promises to reshape industries and everyday life.

title: GasMeth Energy Boosts Investment in Lake Kivu Methane Gas Project to 810 Billion Rwf
excerpt: GasMeth Energy Ltd, a company extracting methane gas from Lake Kivu, has announced an additional 230 billion Rwf investment into its gas extraction and processing operations, bringing its total investment to 810 billion Rwf.
title_en: GasMeth Energy Boosts Investment in Lake Kivu Methane Gas Project to 810 Billion Rwf
excerpt_en: GasMeth Energy Ltd, a company extracting methane gas from Lake Kivu, has announced an additional 230 billion Rwf investment into its gas extraction and processing operations, bringing its total investment to 810 billion Rwf.
body_en:
GasMeth Energy Ltd, a company extracting methane gas from Lake Kivu, has announced an additional 230 billion Rwf investment into its gas extraction and processing operations, bringing its total investment to 810 billion Rwf. The first phase, valued at 522 billion Rwf, aims to supply methane gas for both domestic and industrial use, according to The New Times.

The project stems from a 2019 agreement between the Rwandan government and GasMeth Energy to harness methane gas for cooking, industry, and vehicles. Under the 25-year contract, GasMeth Energy is expected to extract up to 40 million cubic meters of methane per day, enough to supply 300,000 to 400,000 households based on current usage.

On August 18, 2022, the foundation stone for the processing plant was laid in Bwishyura Sector, Karongi District, marking the start of essential construction works. The project has faced challenges in securing investment and sourcing equipment internationally. CEO Stephen Tierney noted that delays were partly due to the need to secure buyers for the gas before raising sufficient capital, as well as slow delivery of key machinery from abroad.

“This time, the onshore and offshore works are almost complete. The underwater works have also begun,” Tierney said.

Supported by the Rwandan government and institutions such as Afreximbank, the plant has already employed 250 workers, with plans to expand the workforce to 800 by next year.

The project aligns with Rwanda’s push for environmentally friendly cooking fuels. According to the Seventh Household Income and Expenditure Survey (EICV7), households using clean fuels increased from 1% in 2017 to 5.4% in 2024. The survey highlights that 75% of households still rely on firewood, 18.8% use charcoal, and 5.4% use gas, biogas, or electricity. In Kigali, 23% of households use gas, compared to 59% using charcoal and 17% using wood.

GasMeth Energy will become the third company producing methane gas from Lake Kivu, following KivuWatt and Shema Power Lake Kivu, further strengthening Rwanda’s efforts to expand clean energy access and reduce dependence on traditional biomass fuels.

title: Rwanda’s Insurance Sector Surpasses 1,000 Billion Rwf, Eyes Further Growth
excerpt: KIGALI - Rwanda’s insurance sector has more than doubled in value over the past six years, reaching 1,212.3 billion Rwf as of June 2025, according to statistics from the Central Bank of Rwanda (BNR).
title_en: Rwanda’s Insurance Sector Surpasses 1,000 Billion Rwf, Eyes Further Growth
excerpt_en: KIGALI - Rwanda’s insurance sector has more than doubled in value over the past six years, reaching 1,212.3 billion Rwf as of June 2025, according to statistics from the Central Bank of Rwanda (BNR).
body_en:
KIGALI - Rwanda’s insurance sector has more than doubled in value over the past six years, reaching 1,212.3 billion Rwf as of June 2025, according to statistics from the Central Bank of Rwanda (BNR). In 2019, the sector was valued at 505.6 billion Rwf, highlighting significant growth in recent years.

The sector saw an increase of 71 billion Rwf in just six months, rising from 1,141.1 billion Rwf in December 2024. BNR data indicates that 18 insurance companies currently operate in Rwanda, including 16 private firms and two public institutions - RSSB and MMI, which provide health insurance.

Among these, nine companies offer non-health insurance, three provide health coverage, and others specialize in low-income insurance, institutional insurance, medical insurance, and mutual health insurance (Mutuelle de Santé). The sector also comprises 14 insurance intermediaries, two supplementary insurance intermediaries, 11 bank insurance providers, 1,661 insurance agents, 32 loss adjusters, and six actuaries.

Growth has been driven by Gross Written Premiums, rising capital, and increased profits from investments. In state-owned insurers, premiums increased from 121.5 billion Rwf in December 2023 to 135.2 billion Rwf in December 2024, while non-state insurers saw premiums climb from 177.1 billion Rwf to 216.1 billion Rwf over the same period.

Motor insurance led growth in non-life coverage, rising by 26.2% to 67.6 billion Rwf in December 2024. Government bonds account for 33.2% of total sector assets, while 44% are invested in financial institutions such as commercial banks.

The Ministry of Finance and Economic Planning notes that general insurance remains the most popular product, accounting for 49% of all insurance, followed by motor insurance at 20%, long-term life insurance at 12%, medical insurance at 11%, and property insurance at 6%.

Currently, the insurance sector represents 1.9% of Rwanda’s GDP, with projections to reach 3.2% by 2029. BNR Governor Soraya Hakuziyaremye said reforms planned over the next decade aim to expand coverage and modernize the sector.

“We have a new strategy that will outline a comprehensive plan for insurance in Rwanda. It will encourage and educate the population to use insurance services and explore the introduction of new insurance products,” she told RBA.

In 2024, 27% of Rwandan adults held insurance policies beyond mutual health insurance, up from 17% (1.2 million people) in 2020, indicating growing uptake of insurance services nationwide.

title: Rwanda Eyes 1,084 Billion Rwf Investment as Kigali Positions Itself as African Financial Hub
excerpt: KIGALI, RWANDA - Rwanda is steadily advancing its ambition to become a leading financial hub in Africa through the Kigali International Financial Centre (KIFC), with expectations for investment in the sector to reach…
title_en: Rwanda Eyes 1,084 Billion Rwf Investment as Kigali Positions Itself as African Financial Hub
excerpt_en: KIGALI, RWANDA - Rwanda is steadily advancing its ambition to become a leading financial hub in Africa through the Kigali International Financial Centre (KIFC), with expectations for investment in the sector to reach…
body_en:
KIGALI, RWANDA - Rwanda is steadily advancing its ambition to become a leading financial hub in Africa through the Kigali International Financial Centre (KIFC), with expectations for investment in the sector to reach 1,084 billion Rwf by 2029.

According to the Financial Sector Development Strategy 2025-2030, KIFC aims to double both the number of international investors in Rwanda and the registered assets under its management. Assets are projected to grow from 64 billion Rwf in 2023 to 133.76 billion Rwf by 2029, marking a 109% increase. Annual targets include 91.9 billion Rwf in 2025/26, 105.85 billion Rwf in 2026/27, and 119.8 billion Rwf in 2027/28.

The number of international investors is expected to rise from 140 in 2023 to nearly 293 in 2029. Similarly, the total value of registered investor assets is projected to climb from 519 billion Rwf in 2024 to 1,084 billion Rwf by 2028/29, with incremental growth reaching 745 billion in 2025/26, 858 billion in 2026/27, and 972 billion in 2027/28.

Launched in 2020, KIFC allows investors to base their decision-making in Rwanda while operating businesses internationally. Investors can use Rwandan banks for capital deployment, ensuring their financial activities remain anchored in the country even if operations extend abroad. This approach aligns with Rwanda’s Vision 2050 to position Kigali as a continental financial hub.

KIFC provides investors with confidence through legal frameworks, tax incentives, and a growing network of double taxation agreements, which are set to increase from 13 to at least 28 by 2029. The centre currently ranks third in Africa and second in Sub-Saharan Africa, having registered about 40 new investors in 2023 alone.

International partnerships have been established with institutions in Casablanca, Jersey, Luxembourg, Qatar, and Singapore to foster cooperation, expand investment opportunities, and enhance financial sector skills. However, Rwanda acknowledges areas for improvement, including promoting KIFC at global forums, modernizing financial laws, encouraging innovation, and increasing the number of certified financial professionals. Currently, only 2% of the 40,000-strong workforce holds international financial certifications.

Rwanda’s stable investment environment, strong anti-corruption record, and access to a regional market of over 838 million people continue to attract investors. Notable projects include the Virunga Africa Fund 1, valued at over $250 million, supporting private sector development, and the Fund for African Development (FEDA), headquartered in Kigali with $670 million earmarked for various projects. Mauritius-based financial services firm DTOS has also launched operations in Rwanda to provide financing and guarantees for investors.

Through KIFC, Rwanda continues to position itself as a strategic gateway for financial investment in Africa, reinforcing its role as a secure and investor-friendly destination.

title: Rwanda: Unemployment Falls to 13.4% as Job Opportunities Grow
excerpt: KIGALI, Rwanda - Unemployment in Rwanda has dropped to 13.4% in the third quarter of 2025, marking a 1.9% decline compared to the same period in 2024, according to the National Institute of Statistics of Rwanda (NISR).
title_en: Rwanda: Unemployment Falls to 13.4% as Job Opportunities Grow
excerpt_en: KIGALI, Rwanda - Unemployment in Rwanda has dropped to 13.4% in the third quarter of 2025, marking a 1.9% decline compared to the same period in 2024, according to the National Institute of Statistics of Rwanda (NISR).
body_en:
KIGALI, Rwanda - Unemployment in Rwanda has dropped to 13.4% in the third quarter of 2025, marking a 1.9% decline compared to the same period in 2024, according to the National Institute of Statistics of Rwanda (NISR). The latest survey shows that roughly one in seven people in the labor market remains unemployed.

NISR data indicate that unemployment remains higher among women, at 15.9%, compared to 11.2% for men. Youth unemployment stands at 15.5%, while 11.7% of adults are without work. The survey also reveals a rural-urban divide, with rural areas recording 14.2% unemployment versus 11.8% in urban centers.

Rwanda has a working-age population of 8,571,278, with 5,643,232 people - or 65.8% - active in the labor market, a 1.7% increase from the third quarter of 2024. Of these, 4,888,921, or 57%, are employed, up from 54.3% in the same quarter last year.

The NISR report notes progress across both genders, with employment among men rising 1.8% and among women by 3.6%. Women now make up 49% of the employed population, while men account for 66.1%, narrowing the employment gap to 17.1% from 18.9% in 2024.

Age also plays a role in employment patterns. The majority of employed Rwandans are over 31 years old (57.3%), while those aged 16 to 30 account for 56.6% of employed individuals. Sector-wise, 44.9% of employed Rwandans work in services, 35.1% in agriculture, and 20% in industry. Among the unemployed, 53.7% are involved in subsistence agriculture, while 46.3% are not engaged in any productive activity.

Of the working-age population, 34.2% are not part of the labor market, a slight decrease from 35.9% in 2024. However, 56.7% of Rwandans are reported to not fully utilize their potential through underemployment or working in jobs that do not match their skills - a challenge more pronounced among women (64.7%) than men (48.3%). Youth underutilization stands at 57.8%, while 55.8% of adults are similarly affected.

Over the past five years, Rwanda has seen a steady decline in unemployment, from 19.4% in 2021 to 18.1% in 2022, 18% in 2023, and 15.3% in 2024, reaching 13.4% in the third quarter of 2025. Employment rates have concurrently risen from 41% in 2021 to 57% in 2025, reflecting a positive trend in job creation and labor market participation.

The survey underscores Rwanda’s ongoing efforts to boost employment and optimize the potential of its working-age population as the country continues its economic growth trajectory.

title: Rubavu: Lake Kivu Methane Monitoring Laboratory Completes 80% of Construction
excerpt: RUBAVU, Rwanda - Construction of a 2 billion Rwandan franc laboratory to monitor methane in Lake Kivu is now 80% complete, the Rwanda Environment Management Agency (REMA) announced.
title_en: Rubavu: Lake Kivu Methane Monitoring Laboratory Completes 80% of Construction
excerpt_en: RUBAVU, Rwanda - Construction of a 2 billion Rwandan franc laboratory to monitor methane in Lake Kivu is now 80% complete, the Rwanda Environment Management Agency (REMA) announced.
body_en:
RUBAVU, Rwanda - Construction of a 2 billion Rwandan franc laboratory to monitor methane in Lake Kivu is now 80% complete, the Rwanda Environment Management Agency (REMA) announced. The facility is expected to be finalized in November and inaugurated the following month.

Located in the Rubavu district, this laboratory is part of the Lake Kivu Monitoring Program (LKMP). It will be equipped with state-of-the-art equipment for monitoring water and gas quality and protecting the environment, while also serving as a research center for scientists in biology, chemistry, and earth sciences, providing access to equipment rarely available in the region.

Eric Mudakikwa Ruhanamirindi, head of the Lake Kivu monitoring unit at REMA, stated before the Rwandan Parliament's Committee on Land, Agriculture, Livestock, and Environmental Conservation: "The main objective is to study how to extract methane while protecting the environment."

Alex Mugabo, coordinator of REMA's project implementation unit, explained that the work is progressing well, despite a shortfall of 500 to 600 million Rwandan francs to complete the project. According to him, the necessary funds have already been secured, which will allow the work to be completed smoothly.

Lake Kivu contains between 60 and 70 cubic kilometers of methane, of which 44.7 cubic kilometers are exploitable. It is also used for transportation, fishing, tourism, and water sports.

Rwanda currently operates two methane extraction plants, KivuWatt and Shema Power Lake Kivu, and a third, GasMeth, will soon be commissioned. Over the next five years, the country plans to invest more than one billion dollars to produce 1,000 megawatts of electricity, including 136 megawatts from methane, to support various national activities.

This laboratory is expected to strengthen local scientific research and contribute to the sustainable management of Lake Kivu, a strategic resource for Rwanda.

title: Rwanda, Saudi Arabia Launch Project to Distribute 50,000 Cooking Gas Cylinders and Stoves
excerpt: Rwanda, in partnership with Saudi Arabia, has launched a joint initiative to provide 50,000 households with cooking gas cylinders and stoves, marking a significant step toward cleaner, safer, and more sustainable…
title_en: Rwanda, Saudi Arabia Launch Project to Distribute 50,000 Cooking Gas Cylinders and Stoves
excerpt_en: Rwanda, in partnership with Saudi Arabia, has launched a joint initiative to provide 50,000 households with cooking gas cylinders and stoves, marking a significant step toward cleaner, safer, and more sustainable…
body_en:
Rwanda, in partnership with Saudi Arabia, has launched a joint initiative to provide 50,000 households with cooking gas cylinders and stoves, marking a significant step toward cleaner, safer, and more sustainable cooking solutions.

The project, unveiled under Saudi Arabia’s Forward7 Program, is part of the broader Middle East Green Initiative launched in 2021. It aims to help Rwandan families transition from traditional biomass fuels-such as firewood and charcoal-to modern Liquefied Petroleum Gas (LPG) systems that are more environmentally friendly and health-conscious.

According to a joint statement issued on October 29, 2025, by Rwanda’s Ministry of Infrastructure and Forward7, each beneficiary household will receive a two-burner stove, a 12-kilogram gas cylinder, and an affordability device that allows users to pay for gas in small increments. This feature is designed to support lower-income families who may not be able to purchase a full gas refill at once.

The project, which will run over 18 months, is being implemented by Bboxx, a company known for its work in renewable energy distribution across Africa. So far, since its pilot phase began in February 2025, the program has already reached 6,000 households, with plans to expand into Kigali, Huye, Muhanga, Rwamagana, and Musanze districts.

Government data shows that the majority of Rwandan households still rely on biomass for cooking-75% use firewood, 18.8% use charcoal, and only 5.4% use gas or biogas. In Kigali, however, 23% of households use gas, while 59% depend on charcoal.

Officials say the program will play a crucial role in reducing Rwanda’s dependence on wood-based fuels, which contribute to deforestation and indoor air pollution. It will also support the country’s participation in the carbon credit market, which rewards projects that reduce greenhouse gas emissions. The resulting funds will be reinvested in renewable energy initiatives nationwide.

The shift toward clean cooking is a cornerstone of Rwanda’s broader climate and energy goals. The government is also advancing a major project to extract 40 million cubic meters of methane gas from Lake Kivu, which is expected to supply gas to 300,000-400,000 households for cooking.

Through partnerships like this, Rwanda aims to make modern energy solutions accessible to all citizens while meeting its commitment to reduce greenhouse gas emissions and promote sustainable development.

According to a joint statement issued on October 29, 2025, by Rwanda’s Ministry of Infrastructure and Forward7, each beneficiary household will receive a two-burner stove, a 12-kilogram gas cylinder, and an affordability device that allows users to pay for gas in small increments. This feature is designed to support lower-income families who may not be able to purchase a full gas refill at once.

The project, which will run over 18 months, is being implemented by Bboxx, a company known for its work in renewable energy distribution across Africa. So far, since its pilot phase began in February 2025, the program has already reached 6,000 households, with plans to expand into Kigali, Huye, Muhanga, Rwamagana, and Musanze districts.

Government data shows that the majority of Rwandan households still rely on biomass for cooking-75% use firewood, 18.8% use charcoal, and only 5.4% use gas or biogas. In Kigali, however, 23% of households use gas, while 59% depend on charcoal.

Officials say the program will play a crucial role in reducing Rwanda’s dependence on wood-based fuels, which contribute to deforestation and indoor air pollution. It will also support the country’s participation in the carbon credit market, which rewards projects that reduce greenhouse gas emissions. The resulting funds will be reinvested in renewable energy initiatives nationwide.

The shift toward clean cooking is a cornerstone of Rwanda’s broader climate and energy goals. The government is also advancing a major project to extract 40 million cubic meters of methane gas from Lake Kivu, which is expected to supply gas to 300,000-400,000 households for cooking.

Through partnerships like this, Rwanda aims to make modern energy solutions accessible to all citizens while meeting its commitment to reduce greenhouse gas emissions and promote sustainable development.

title: Karongi District Achieves 96% Access to Clean Water as Rwanda Targets Full Coverage by 2029
excerpt: Access to clean water in Karongi District has reached 96%, marking a major milestone in Rwanda’s national goal of ensuring universal access to safe drinking water by 2029, according to local officials.
title_en: Karongi District Achieves 96% Access to Clean Water as Rwanda Targets Full Coverage by 2029
excerpt_en: Access to clean water in Karongi District has reached 96%, marking a major milestone in Rwanda’s national goal of ensuring universal access to safe drinking water by 2029, according to local officials.
body_en:
Access to clean water in Karongi District has reached 96%, marking a major milestone in Rwanda’s national goal of ensuring universal access to safe drinking water by 2029, according to local officials.

Residents are considered to have access to clean water if they live within 500 meters of a water tap in rural areas or 200 meters in urban settings.

During the end-of-October community service (Umuganda) event attended by Prime Minister Dr. Justin Nsengiyumva, the Mayor of Karongi District, Muzungu Gelard, praised the government’s efforts to expand water infrastructure across the district.

“We have reached a satisfactory level in terms of access to clean water,” he said. “The upcoming Kivu Belt Water Supply System will further extend access to several sectors in Karongi town.”

Residents have already begun to see the impact of these projects. Mukantabana Xaverine, from Rugabano Sector, shared how the new water connections have improved daily life.“We didn’t have clean water before. We had to walk down to the valley for 30 minutes to fetch water, and carrying a 20-liter jerrycan uphill was exhausting,” she said. “Now that water is nearby, I can bathe and wash clothes regularly. Before, we could go two or three days without bathing just to save water.”

The Acting Director of the National Water, Sanitation and Hygiene Agency (WASAC) in Karongi, Niyishimwa Fidèle, confirmed that clean water access in the district now stands at 96%. He attributed the success largely to the Karongi WASH Project, a partnership between the District and Water for People, which has been active in all 13 sectors since 2020.

“I think there is no place in Karongi where you can’t find a water source,” Niyishimwa noted. “Our next step is to increase supply capacity, which is why we are completing a water treatment plant that is now 85% finished.”

Looking ahead, officials are confident that the Kivu Belt Water Supply System, set to begin soon, will help achieve 100% clean water access in Karongi by 2029.

This achievement underscores Rwanda’s broader commitment to improving public health, sanitation, and quality of life through sustainable water infrastructure development.

title: Rwanda Trains 150 Teachers on Artificial Intelligence to Transform Education
excerpt: KIGALI, Rwanda - Rwanda is stepping up its use of artificial intelligence (AI) in education, with more than 150 teachers trained to integrate AI into classrooms, the Minister of Education, Joseph Nsengimana, announced…
title_en: Rwanda Trains 150 Teachers on Artificial Intelligence to Transform Education
excerpt_en: KIGALI, Rwanda - Rwanda is stepping up its use of artificial intelligence (AI) in education, with more than 150 teachers trained to integrate AI into classrooms, the Minister of Education, Joseph Nsengimana, announced…
body_en:
KIGALI, Rwanda - Rwanda is stepping up its use of artificial intelligence (AI) in education, with more than 150 teachers trained to integrate AI into classrooms, the Minister of Education, Joseph Nsengimana, announced at the Mobile World Congress 2025.

The training is part of the government’s ongoing implementation of the ICT Policy, approved two years ago, aimed at harnessing technology to improve learning outcomes and address challenges such as school overcrowding.

Minister Nsengimana explained that AI will assist in monitoring and supporting students, particularly in schools facing a shortage of teachers. “AI will be used to help students when we have a shortage of teachers, because it will allow more students to be monitored in a shorter time than one teacher could do,” he said.

The initial cohort of 150 teachers-five from each district-will serve as trainers for their peers, ensuring a nationwide rollout of AI in classrooms. The Minister added that AI-powered smart technology is expected to begin being used in schools next year.

Currently, Rwanda has 107,741 teachers across kindergartens, primary, and secondary schools, including 50,468 men and 57,273 women. The government has already introduced AI in other sectors, including health, research, and agriculture, where it is used for tasks such as pest control, irrigation, and monitoring.

This initiative marks a significant step in Rwanda’s efforts to modernize its education system, enhance teaching efficiency, and prepare students for a future driven by technology.

title: Rwanda FDA approves Africa’s first low-cost eye disease drug
excerpt: KIGALI - The Rwanda Food and Drugs Authority (FDA) has approved the sale of BioUcenta™, a low-cost drug for treating eye diseases, marking the first time the medication has reached Africa.
title_en: Rwanda FDA approves Africa’s first low-cost eye disease drug
excerpt_en: KIGALI - The Rwanda Food and Drugs Authority (FDA) has approved the sale of BioUcenta™, a low-cost drug for treating eye diseases, marking the first time the medication has reached Africa.
body_en:
KIGALI - The Rwanda Food and Drugs Authority (FDA) has approved the sale of BioUcenta™, a low-cost drug for treating eye diseases, marking the first time the medication has reached Africa. The drug will be manufactured by US-based biotech company Bio Usawa, under marketing authorization from Bioeq AG in Switzerland.

BioUcenta™, similar in efficacy to Lucentis® produced by Swiss company Genentech, treats conditions such as diabetic macular edema, Age-related Macular Degeneration (AMD), and diabetic retinopathy, all of which can cause vision loss. The approved drug is expected to arrive in Rwanda in 2026 and will be 80% cheaper than its counterpart, making it more accessible to patients in the region.

“This approval is a major step forward for Bio Usawa and demonstrates Rwanda’s commitment to helping patients access modern medicine,” said Dr. Menghis Bairu, President of Bio Usawa.

Ophthalmologist and co-founder of the Rwanda International Institute of Ophthalmology (RIIO), Prof. Ciku Mathenge, called the approval a milestone for healthcare in Africa. “For a long time, doctors struggled with the lack of timely access to these medicines, while patients suffered due to high costs. Rwanda is taking the lead in developing access to modern medicines,” he said.

Bio Usawa, known for manufacturing vaccines and other advanced medicines, signed an agreement with the Rwanda Development Board (RDB) in November 2024 to establish the country’s first pharmaceutical factory. The facility will initially focus on eye disease treatments before expanding to medicines for cancer and other serious conditions.

Rwanda is positioning itself as a regional hub for healthcare, promoting local pharmaceutical production and improving access to essential medicines for its population and beyond.

title: Rwanda’s Forensic Institute Processes Nearly 100,000 Cases in Seven Years
excerpt: The National Institute for Forensic Science and Technology (RFI) has announced that it has processed 96,989 forensic evidence files since its establishment seven years ago.
title_en: Rwanda’s Forensic Institute Processes Nearly 100,000 Cases in Seven Years
excerpt_en: The National Institute for Forensic Science and Technology (RFI) has announced that it has processed 96,989 forensic evidence files since its establishment seven years ago.
body_en:
The National Institute for Forensic Science and Technology (RFI) has announced that it has processed 96,989 forensic evidence files since its establishment seven years ago. The milestone was revealed on October 28, 2025, in Nyamata Sector, Bugesera District, during the ongoing public awareness campaign “Sobanukirwa RFI” - an initiative designed to help citizens understand the institute’s services and their role in ensuring justice.

According to SP Ashimirwe Japhet, RFI’s Branch Manager, forensic science services in Rwanda began within the Rwanda National Police in 2005 before evolving into a separate laboratory. In 2016, a law officially established RFI as a national forensic institution, and by 2018, it began full operations.

Initially focused on judicial cases, RFI expanded its scope in 2023 to provide services to non-judicial sectors, extending its reach to both Rwandans and foreign clients.

SP Ashimirwe explained that the institute plays a key role in supporting investigations and upholding justice through scientific evidence. The Sobanukirwa RFI campaign, he said, was born out of recommendations from the National Dialogue Council, aiming to make citizens aware of the role forensic science plays in resolving cases.

Dr. Kabera Justin, head of the Drug Testing Department, emphasized RFI’s mission to ensure that “every Rwandan can receive justice based on scientific evidence.” He noted that citizens often encounter situations - such as cases of violence or disputes - where forensic testing is essential for fair outcomes.

During the session, local leaders were briefed on the institute’s services and pledged to strengthen community awareness. Bugesera Mayor, Mutabazi Richard, said the district would help residents better understand how to access RFI services, adding:

“We will ensure that citizens know that no one should be deprived of justice that requires forensic evidence. We will connect them with those responsible.”

Through these services, RFI continues to strengthen scientific-based justice in Rwanda, ensuring that legal and investigative decisions rely on evidence rather than speculation.

title: Trial Begins for 16 Nyabihu District Officials Accused of Embezzlement, Entrepreneur Absent
excerpt: The Nyabihu District Court has commenced hearings against 16 district officials accused of embezzling public funds, including the Executive Secretary of Nyabihu District, David Mugiraneza, and the Director of the…
title_en: Trial Begins for 16 Nyabihu District Officials Accused of Embezzlement, Entrepreneur Absent
excerpt_en: The Nyabihu District Court has commenced hearings against 16 district officials accused of embezzling public funds, including the Executive Secretary of Nyabihu District, David Mugiraneza, and the Director of the…
body_en:
The Nyabihu District Court has commenced hearings against 16 district officials accused of embezzling public funds, including the Executive Secretary of Nyabihu District, David Mugiraneza, and the Director of the Department of Social Welfare. The case also involves the President of IBUKA in Nyabihu and leaders from seven sectors-Jenda, Bigogwe, Mukamira, Muringa, Rugera, Kintobo, and Rambura-connected to a project to build 17 houses for genocide survivors. The hearing began on Tuesday, October 28, 2025, at Mukamira District Court.

The prosecution presented the charges against each defendant from 10:05 a.m. to 10:50 a.m., requesting 30 days of temporary detention for crimes punishable by over two years in prison. The officials are accused of failing to complete the houses due to missing construction materials, and then falsely claiming that the contractor had delivered the supplies.

Mr. Mugiraneza faces two charges, including confirming that the buildings were complete and misusing public funds. The prosecution also alleged that evidence was destroyed or obstructed during the investigation.

From 10:51 a.m. until 5:12 p.m., 15 of the defendants defended themselves individually, leaving three to continue their defense later. The District Executive Secretary denied both charges, arguing that his actions were in the interest of the district, not personal gain.

“The building officer indicated that the 10 houses included in the contract were 100% complete and were being transferred to the authorities, showing the contract was abandoned and done in the district’s interest,” Mugiraneza stated.“I was the first to follow up on these reports. In July, I summoned all IBUKA Presidents regarding the seven unfinished buildings; they were the ones requested to receive 6 million Rwf to complete them from the budget to help the needy.”

Lawyers defending Mugiraneza highlighted that he had three guarantors with assets worth 60 million Rwf, and that the 6 million Rwf transfer was based on a technical document still held at the sectors. They argued that this did not justify detention.

All arguments concluded at 6:46 p.m., with the judge scheduling the detention and provisional release decision for October 30, 2025, at 3:00 p.m. Meanwhile, the defendants, who had been under investigation in Kigali for several days, were detained at the Jenda RIB Station pending the court’s ruling.

The trial is closely watched, as it involves officials responsible for overseeing funds meant to support survivors of the Genocide against the Tutsi, highlighting ongoing efforts to ensure accountability in public service.

title: Huye: Over 300 Bodies Believed to Be Victims of 1994 Genocide Found in Four Months
excerpt: Huye District authorities and the Ibuka Community have announced the discovery of more than 300 bodies in Matyazo Cell, Ngoma Sector, believed to be victims of the 1994 Genocide against the Tutsi.
title_en: Huye: Over 300 Bodies Believed to Be Victims of 1994 Genocide Found in Four Months
excerpt_en: Huye District authorities and the Ibuka Community have announced the discovery of more than 300 bodies in Matyazo Cell, Ngoma Sector, believed to be victims of the 1994 Genocide against the Tutsi.
body_en:
Huye District authorities and the Ibuka Community have announced the discovery of more than 300 bodies in Matyazo Cell, Ngoma Sector, believed to be victims of the 1994 Genocide against the Tutsi. The findings, reported between June and October 2025, were made in the villages of Kamucuzi, Rurenda, and Kamatyazo, with some remains uncovered in fields and others buried under structures.

“Most of the people living in Matyazo are immigrants. Those who lived there before the genocide either fled or were killed. Many of the current residents bought land later, and it is often from their backyards that bodies are being discovered,” said Siboyintore Théodate, President of Ibuka in Huye District.

The discoveries include 46 bodies found in August at the farm of Munyempamo Faustin, nicknamed Gérard, 92 bodies in early September at the Gasarasi farm, and more than 180 bodies in October alone. These sites are near locations where over 2,000 bodies were found in 2023 and another 1,200 before April 2025.

Siboyintore explained that many of the victims came from other regions, including Nyaruguru, Karama, and Gikongoro, and were killed in areas along the many roads and checkpoints in Matyazo during the genocide.

“The truth about these mass graves came from testimonies of survivors and witnesses who provided detailed accounts during the 31st Kwibuka commemoration at ADEPR Matyazo. Their accounts guided us to the locations where bodies were buried,” he added.

Ibuka and local authorities continue to urge residents with information on undiscovered burial sites to come forward to ensure that the victims are laid to rest with dignity.

Over the past two years, more than 3,500 bodies have been recovered in Ngoma and Matyazo cells-over 2,000 in 2024, more than 1,200 in May 2025, and now over 300 in the recent months, with the number still rising.

The ongoing discoveries highlight the continued efforts to document and honor the victims of the 1994 Genocide, even decades later, and underscore the importance of community cooperation in locating burial sites.

title: ‘Be One Gin’ Factory Owner Arrested Over Alleged Dangerous Alcohol Production
excerpt: KIGALI - Habumugisha Jean Paul, owner of Roots Investment Group, the company behind ‘Be One Gin’, has been arrested as authorities investigate allegations that his products endanger public health.
title_en: ‘Be One Gin’ Factory Owner Arrested Over Alleged Dangerous Alcohol Production
excerpt_en: KIGALI - Habumugisha Jean Paul, owner of Roots Investment Group, the company behind ‘Be One Gin’, has been arrested as authorities investigate allegations that his products endanger public health.
body_en:
KIGALI - Habumugisha Jean Paul, owner of Roots Investment Group, the company behind ‘Be One Gin’, has been arrested as authorities investigate allegations that his products endanger public health. His case has been forwarded to the Prosecution Service as investigators gather evidence for formal charges, officials confirmed.

The arrest follows Operation ‘Usalama XI’, conducted between October 15-17, 2025, which targeted unsafe alcohol production across the country.

Dr. Murangira B. Thierry, spokesperson for the National Bureau of Investigation (RBI), told IGIHE, “It is true that Habumugisha Jean Paul, owner of the ‘Be One Gin’ factory, has been arrested and his case has been forwarded to the Prosecution Service. He is suspected of producing drinks that can kill or endanger life.”

Habumugisha is currently held at the Rusororo RIB Station. He faces charges under Article 115 of the Rwandan Penal Code, which criminalizes the distribution of substances that may cause illness or incapacitation, even if there was no intent to kill.

If convicted, he could face two to three years in prison and a fine ranging from 300,000 to 500,000 Rwandan francs. Authorities have urged the public to exercise caution when consuming unregulated alcohol products.

title: Karongi: Over 60 Arrested in 10 Months for Role in the Genocide
excerpt: KARONGI - In the past 10 months, authorities in Karongi District have arrested over 60 individuals implicated in the 1994 Genocide against the Tutsi, the District Administration announced.
title_en: Karongi: Over 60 Arrested in 10 Months for Role in the Genocide
excerpt_en: KARONGI - In the past 10 months, authorities in Karongi District have arrested over 60 individuals implicated in the 1994 Genocide against the Tutsi, the District Administration announced.
body_en:
KARONGI - In the past 10 months, authorities in Karongi District have arrested over 60 individuals implicated in the 1994 Genocide against the Tutsi, the District Administration announced. Many of those apprehended had previously evaded justice after being convicted by the Gacaca courts.

Since January 2025, the district, in collaboration with the Rwanda National Police, National Criminal Investigation Service (RIB), and the IBUKA Association, has intensified efforts to locate and apprehend genocide perpetrators who fled their homes following conviction.

Umuhoza Pascasie, Deputy Mayor of Karongi in charge of Community Welfare, emphasized the importance of addressing the ideology of genocide and helping those who served sentences understand the lasting impact of their crimes. “There are those who have completed their sentences and returned home feeling released from their debt, but in reality, there is no compensation for taking a life. They must understand the lasting debt to the nation and the victims,” he said.

Umuhoza added that ongoing efforts also focus on locating convicted individuals who escaped justice, noting, “We have already arrested about 60, others are still being sought across the country, in collaboration with other institutions.”

Ngarambe Vedaste, President of the Karongi District Council and IBUKA in the district, said that in the former Kibuye Prefecture, more than 300,000 people were convicted for their role in the genocide. He highlighted that while many have served their sentences, others remain at large. “We thank residents for providing information on those we know, and we will continue searching for and arresting them,” Ngarambe said.

Most of those arrested were found after fleeing from Ngoma and Kirehe districts in the Eastern Province, with others apprehended in Kigali City and the Northern Province. Plans are underway to exchange and verify lists of individuals who moved between Kibuye, Ngoma, and Kirehe to ensure those involved in the genocide are brought to justice.

title: Karongi: Teenager Kills Father Following Family Dispute
excerpt: KARONGI, RWANDA - A 16-year-old boy from Karongi District is now wanted after fatally attacking his 62-year-old father in Nyarubuye Village, Gacaca Cell, Rubengera Sector on October 26, 2025.
title_en: Karongi: Teenager Kills Father Following Family Dispute
excerpt_en: KARONGI, RWANDA - A 16-year-old boy from Karongi District is now wanted after fatally attacking his 62-year-old father in Nyarubuye Village, Gacaca Cell, Rubengera Sector on October 26, 2025.
body_en:
KARONGI, RWANDA - A 16-year-old boy from Karongi District is now wanted after fatally attacking his 62-year-old father in Nyarubuye Village, Gacaca Cell, Rubengera Sector on October 26, 2025. Authorities say the incident stemmed from ongoing family tensions, including harassment of the boy’s mother that had led to a divorce two years prior.

According to reports, the teenager confronted his father around 3:00 am. A fight ensued, and the boy struck his father with a plowshare while the man was outside. He then fled the scene. Neighbors found the father unconscious and immediately alerted authorities.

Uwiringiyimana Bosco, Executive Secretary of Gacaca Cell, confirmed that local authorities and the police, including the Rwandan Investigation Bureau (RIB), are actively searching for the suspect. “We are still looking for the suspect, but he has not been arrested. We urge the public to avoid violence and report any disputes so that authorities can assist in resolving them,” he said.

The deceased leaves behind a wife and four children, including the teenager. Local officials are appealing to the community to provide information on the boy’s whereabouts to aid the investigation.

title: Nyamasheke Prison: Shots Fired to Quell Minor Rebellion
excerpt: NYAMASHEKE, RWANDA - Shots were fired in the air at Nyamasheke Prison on October 26, 2025, after a small group of inmates attempted to rebel against prison rules, the Rwanda Correctional Service (RCS) confirmed.
title_en: Nyamasheke Prison: Shots Fired to Quell Minor Rebellion
excerpt_en: NYAMASHEKE, RWANDA - Shots were fired in the air at Nyamasheke Prison on October 26, 2025, after a small group of inmates attempted to rebel against prison rules, the Rwanda Correctional Service (RCS) confirmed.
body_en:
NYAMASHEKE, RWANDA - Shots were fired in the air at Nyamasheke Prison on October 26, 2025, after a small group of inmates attempted to rebel against prison rules, the Rwanda Correctional Service (RCS) confirmed.

RCS spokesperson, Commissioner Superintendent Hillary Sengabo, told IGIHE that the incident involved around six prisoners who resisted standard search operations. “All prisons in the world have gangs. Sometimes a few inmates may refuse to be searched or misbehave. It is generally bad behavior,” he explained.

Sengabo added that disciplinary measures are being enforced to ensure respect for the institution’s regulations. He confirmed that order has since been restored and that no injuries were reported.

Nyamasheke Prison currently houses 885 men, including inmates serving various sentences and a small number serving life imprisonment. The RCS emphasized that such incidents are common during searches and are handled to maintain safety and order.

title: Nyamagabe: 223 Genocide Convicts Undergo Training on Unity and National Heritage
excerpt: NYAMAGABE, Rwanda - A training program on Unity and National Heritage was launched at Nyamagabe Prison on October 22, 2025, targeting 223 prisoners convicted of crimes during the Genocide against the Tutsi.
title_en: Nyamagabe: 223 Genocide Convicts Undergo Training on Unity and National Heritage
excerpt_en: NYAMAGABE, Rwanda - A training program on Unity and National Heritage was launched at Nyamagabe Prison on October 22, 2025, targeting 223 prisoners convicted of crimes during the Genocide against the Tutsi.
body_en:
NYAMAGABE, Rwanda - A training program on Unity and National Heritage was launched at Nyamagabe Prison on October 22, 2025, targeting 223 prisoners convicted of crimes during the Genocide against the Tutsi. The initiative aims to prepare inmates for reintegration into Rwandan society while fostering patriotism and preventing recidivism.

The training, organized by the Ministry of Unity and Civic Responsibility (MINUBUMWE) in collaboration with the Rwanda Correctional Service (RCS), was inaugurated by the UN High Commissioner for Unity and Heritage, Marie Alice Kayumba Uwera. Among the participants were 50 women and 173 men serving their sentences.

Addressing the prisoners, Kayumba Uwera urged them to become constructive members of society, emphasizing respect, reconciliation, and the rejection of divisive ideologies. “The advice you will receive here will help you avoid being a source of disruption to the unity and integrity of Rwandans by teaching you to contribute to its continued construction,” she said. “Live in peace with those you find in families that are built on the principles of Rwandanness, characterized by truth and avoidance of recidivism.”

Deputy Commissioner General of the RCS, DCG Rose Muhisoni, highlighted that prisoners are being equipped with skills to improve their lives and contribute to national development. “Take advantage of this opportunity and make the most of it,” he advised. “Use what you have learned to help you in your daily life and to improve your well-being.”

The program, which began in March 2025, targets inmates nearing the end of their sentences and seeks to prepare them for a smooth reintegration into society. Studies on reconciliation indicate that the majority of individuals involved in the Genocide who sought forgiveness have successfully distanced themselves from its ideology and re-established positive relationships with their communities.

RCS data show that Rwanda currently has 120,000 prisoners serving sentences for genocide-related crimes. Of these, 27,662 remained in prison as of 2018, with 8,857 released between 2018 and 2023, and an estimated 8,810 expected to be released from 2023 to 2027.

The initiative underscores Rwanda’s continued commitment to national reconciliation, rehabilitation, and the prevention of future crimes.

title: Rwanda ranks second in Africa for lowest organized crime rate
excerpt: KIGALI - Rwanda has been ranked second in Africa for the lowest rate of organized crime, trailing only the Seychelles, the Minister of Justice and Attorney General, Dr. Emmanuel Ugirashebuja, announced on October 22, 2025.
title_en: Rwanda ranks second in Africa for lowest organized crime rate
excerpt_en: KIGALI - Rwanda has been ranked second in Africa for the lowest rate of organized crime, trailing only the Seychelles, the Minister of Justice and Attorney General, Dr. Emmanuel Ugirashebuja, announced on October 22, 2025.
body_en:
KIGALI - Rwanda has been ranked second in Africa for the lowest rate of organized crime, trailing only the Seychelles, the Minister of Justice and Attorney General, Dr. Emmanuel Ugirashebuja, announced on October 22, 2025. The announcement came during a meeting of the Ministry of Justice and its partners to outline strategies for crime prevention in the 2025/26 financial year.

Dr. Ugirashebuja highlighted that since the 2004 reforms of Rwanda’s justice system, the country has made significant progress in reducing crime, a trend increasingly reflected in reports from local and international institutions. He cited the latest ENACT project rankings, which placed Rwanda 53rd out of 54 African countries in terms of organized crime, just behind the Seychelles, ranked 54th.

The Minister credited the use of technology in justice, including the Integrated Electronic Case Management System (IECMS), with improving access to justice services and increasing the number of cases brought to court. He noted that greater reporting has sometimes revealed higher numbers in certain crimes, such as gender-based violence, which led to the establishment of Isange One Stop Centers.

“Strong measures are required to combat crime globally,” Dr. Ugirashebuja said, noting that the value of technology-related crime rose from $3 trillion in 2015 to $8 trillion in 2023, particularly during the COVID-19 pandemic.

Fatmata Lovetta Sesay, Director of the United Nations Development Programme (UNDP) in Rwanda, emphasized Rwanda’s efforts to fight crime using innovative tools such as drones and community conflict resolution forums. She noted that crimes worldwide are estimated at $5.8 trillion, equivalent to 3-7% of global GDP, but Rwanda is making notable progress.

The Vice-Chancellor for Academics and Research at the Institute of Legal Education and Development (ILPD), Dr. Yves Sezirahiga, revealed that Rwanda requires an estimated 61 billion Rwandan francs annually to effectively fight crime. “We combined strategies from various institutions and consulted finance and planning experts. This study will guide this year’s crime-fighting strategies and outline the technological and institutional capacity needed,” he said.

The meeting underscored the government’s commitment to leveraging technology, improving institutional capacity, and implementing comprehensive strategies to further reduce crime and enhance public safety across Rwanda.

title: Minor crimes dominate Rwandan courts, largely driven by youth, officials say
excerpt: KIGALI - Nearly 70% of cases brought before Rwandan courts involve minor crimes, including theft, assault, and drug-related offenses, the Spokesperson for the Courts, Mutabazi Harrison, revealed on October 22, 2025…
title_en: Minor crimes dominate Rwandan courts, largely driven by youth, officials say
excerpt_en: KIGALI - Nearly 70% of cases brought before Rwandan courts involve minor crimes, including theft, assault, and drug-related offenses, the Spokesperson for the Courts, Mutabazi Harrison, revealed on October 22, 2025…
body_en:
KIGALI - Nearly 70% of cases brought before Rwandan courts involve minor crimes, including theft, assault, and drug-related offenses, the Spokesperson for the Courts, Mutabazi Harrison, revealed on October 22, 2025, during the presentation of the Ministry of Justice’s crime prevention strategies for 2025/26.

“These include minor theft, assault and battery, and drug use. These are the most common crimes in the courts, usually starting in primary courts and then appealing to higher courts,” Mutabazi said, noting that young people are the primary offenders.

He added that while adults in their 40s and 50s are occasionally involved, the majority of cases involve those under 35. “These crimes constitute about 70% of the cases we handle,” he said, highlighting a growing trend in child abuse and technology-related offenses.

Dr. Sezirahiga Yves, Deputy Director for Academic Affairs and Research at the Institute of Legal Education and Development (ILPD), said research shows that vagrancy and unemployment are key drivers of minor crime. “Most youth committing these crimes are unemployed, have dropped out of school, and there is limited coordination between rehabilitation centers and local authorities,” he explained.

Dr. Sezirahiga noted that while rehabilitated individuals are given tools to support themselves professionally, some sell them to survive and later return to crime. Between 2019 and 2023, ILPD data indicates that 289,668 people were admitted to various rehabilitation centers, including temporary shelters, with over 20,000 successfully reintegrated in Iwawa, Gitagata, and Nyamagabe.

Minister of Justice Dr. Emmanuel Ugirashebuja emphasized the importance of early intervention, pointing out that many youth begin offending as children. “The government is working to ensure all children receive education, especially during formative years, which helps prevent crime later in life,” he said.

Officials stressed that tackling vagrancy, improving youth employment, and strengthening rehabilitation programs are critical to reducing minor crimes and fostering safer communities across Rwanda.

title: Director of NI & P Company Ltd hunted for illegal ethanol trading
excerpt: KIGALI - Nizeyuhoraha Pierre, Director of NI & P Company Ltd, is being pursued by Rwandan authorities for allegedly trading ethanol illegally, following the release of findings from ‘Operation Usalama’, a multi-agency…
title_en: Director of NI & P Company Ltd hunted for illegal ethanol trading
excerpt_en: KIGALI - Nizeyuhoraha Pierre, Director of NI & P Company Ltd, is being pursued by Rwandan authorities for allegedly trading ethanol illegally, following the release of findings from ‘Operation Usalama’, a multi-agency…
body_en:
KIGALI - Nizeyuhoraha Pierre, Director of NI & P Company Ltd, is being pursued by Rwandan authorities for allegedly trading ethanol illegally, following the release of findings from ‘Operation Usalama’, a multi-agency crackdown on illicit business practices.

Although NI & P Company Ltd held a license to sell ethanol, regulations require it to be sold only to authorized users. Investigators found that the company had violated these rules, distributing the substance to unlicensed buyers. Ethanol, a raw material used in brewing, was reportedly diverted to produce substandard alcoholic beverages, locally known as ‘ibyuma’ and ‘ibuye’, in Nyabihu District.

Dr. Murangira B. Thierry, spokesperson for the Rwanda Investigation Bureau (RIB), warned of the dangers posed by improperly stored ethanol. “This company was found to be in possession of ethanol stored illegally, which could endanger local residents,” he said.

The investigation revealed that Nizeyuhoraha, aware that he was being sought, fled and is currently evading justice. Dr. Murangira appealed to the public for assistance, stating, “Anyone who knows the whereabouts of Pierre Nizeyuhoraha should immediately inform the Police or RIB. Pierre himself is urged to come forward and answer questions regarding these allegations. Remaining in hiding will not prevent justice from reaching him.”

Authorities continue to investigate the case, emphasizing the importance of curbing illegal ethanol distribution to protect public safety.

title: Eight Nyabihu District Leaders Released as Court Probes Embezzlement Case
excerpt: Nyabihu, Rwanda - The Mukamira Primary Court has ordered the release of eight out of sixteen Nyabihu District officials accused of embezzling public funds, while the remaining eight will remain in detention for 30 days…
title_en: Eight Nyabihu District Leaders Released as Court Probes Embezzlement Case
excerpt_en: Nyabihu, Rwanda - The Mukamira Primary Court has ordered the release of eight out of sixteen Nyabihu District officials accused of embezzling public funds, while the remaining eight will remain in detention for 30 days…
body_en:
Nyabihu, Rwanda - The Mukamira Primary Court has ordered the release of eight out of sixteen Nyabihu District officials accused of embezzling public funds, while the remaining eight will remain in detention for 30 days pending further investigation.

The case, involving the alleged mismanagement of funds meant for the construction of 17 houses for survivors of the 1994 Genocide against the Tutsi, began on Tuesday, October 28, 2025. The court delivered its ruling on Thursday evening, October 30.

Among those released is David Mugiraneza, the Executive Secretary of Nyabihu District, and Sylvestre Gahamanyi, an employee in the social welfare department. The court granted them temporary release but ordered the confiscation of their bail until full recovery of the alleged funds.

Others cleared and reinstated to their positions include Silas Habarurema and Alphonse Muhizi (procurement officers), Simon Mutwarangabo (head of social welfare), Jean Claude Nzafashwanayo (school construction officer), and Gustave Uwizeye (land officer for Jenda Sector).

However, the court ordered the 30-day detention of Denis Nsengiyumva, a building permit officer, along with several representatives of IBUKA, the survivors’ association, from the sectors of Bigogwe, Mukamira, Muringa, Rugera, Kintobo, and Rambura. These individuals were allegedly involved in the supervision of the disputed housing project.

According to court findings, those released were not directly linked to the irregularities surrounding the construction project, as the procurement process had not resulted in any awarded tenders. For those under continued detention, the court cited their close involvement in overseeing the construction as grounds for maintaining custody.

The investigation continues as authorities seek to determine how public funds earmarked for genocide survivors’ housing were handled.

title: Body of Rusizi Footballer Missing in Burundi Returned to Rwanda
excerpt: Authorities in Bugarama Sector, Rusizi District, have confirmed that the body of Musirikare Obed, a young Rwandan man who went missing in Burundi, has been returned to Rwanda for burial.
title_en: Body of Rusizi Footballer Missing in Burundi Returned to Rwanda
excerpt_en: Authorities in Bugarama Sector, Rusizi District, have confirmed that the body of Musirikare Obed, a young Rwandan man who went missing in Burundi, has been returned to Rwanda for burial.
body_en:
Authorities in Bugarama Sector, Rusizi District, have confirmed that the body of Musirikare Obed, a young Rwandan man who went missing in Burundi, has been returned to Rwanda for burial.

Musirikare, aged 31, was a football player for the Muganza Training Center team, which competes in Rwanda’s third division. On October 24, 2025, he reportedly drowned in the Rusizi River while attempting to cross from Rwanda to the Democratic Republic of Congo (DRC) to take part in a friendly football match.

His body was swept away by the current and could not be located immediately. Days later, his family learned that the body had been recovered by residents in Buganda, Burundi, and transferred to the Ubuntu Hospital morgue in Bujumbura. Burundian authorities then issued a public notice inviting anyone who might identify the deceased to come forward.

On October 27, Musirikare’s relatives, friends, and local officials from Bugarama gathered at the Ruhwa border post to receive his remains, as burial preparations had already been made. However, when the delegation was informed that the body was en route, they were later told that it had been withheld by the Burundian police, who reportedly requested additional documentation before release.

The family promptly appealed to Rusizi District authorities for assistance in securing the body’s transfer, while the Bugarama Sector administration also sent a formal request to Bujumbura Provincial officials.

Despite assurances, the handover did not take place on October 28, leaving the family in uncertainty for another day. Finally, in the early hours of October 29, 2025, the body was officially repatriated.

“The body was handed over to us at around 4:00 a.m.,” said the Executive Secretary of Bugarama Sector. “Now that we have received it, it will be buried immediately.”

Musirikare Obed is remembered not only as a talented footballer but also as an employee of the Cimerwa cement factory. His death has saddened both his teammates and the local community, who described him as a passionate sportsman and hardworking young man.

title: Colonel Ruhinda’s Wife Denies Abduction Claims, Says She Found Peace in Rwanda
excerpt: The wife of former FDLR commander Colonel Ruvugayimikore Protogene, widely known as Colonel Ruhinda Gaby, has dismissed allegations that she and her family were abducted by the Rwanda Defence Force (RDF).
title_en: Colonel Ruhinda’s Wife Denies Abduction Claims, Says She Found Peace in Rwanda
excerpt_en: The wife of former FDLR commander Colonel Ruvugayimikore Protogene, widely known as Colonel Ruhinda Gaby, has dismissed allegations that she and her family were abducted by the Rwanda Defence Force (RDF).
body_en:
The wife of former FDLR commander Colonel Ruvugayimikore Protogene, widely known as Colonel Ruhinda Gaby, has dismissed allegations that she and her family were abducted by the Rwanda Defence Force (RDF).

Ruhinda, who once led the FDLR’s elite commando unit known as CRAP (Commando de Recherche et d’Action en Profondeur), was killed in December 2023 in Masisi Territory, North Kivu Province of the Democratic Republic of Congo (DRC). His death sparked internal controversy within the FDLR, with some of his former comrades alleging it resulted from an internal plot.

Born in 1970 in Karago Commune, in what is now Nyabihu District, Ruhinda abandoned veterinary studies in 1994 during the Genocide against the Tutsi to undergo military training. When the Rwandan Patriotic Army (RPA) liberated Rwanda, he fled with other militias to eastern DRC, where he joined the ALiR, later renamed the FDLR. Rising through the ranks, he eventually commanded the group’s special forces.

In 2001, Ruhinda married Claudine Mukamana, a 19-year-old Rwandan woman. The couple settled in Masisi and later moved to Rutshuru and Goma. When the AFC/M23 rebel movement took control of Goma in January 2025, Mukamana chose to stay behind with her children while her husband continued to move between conflict zones.

Her decision not to flee sparked suspicion among some FDLR members, who accused her of being a Rwandan spy. Many of the wives of FDLR leaders reportedly severed contact with her. “They changed their phone numbers so I couldn’t reach them,” she told KT Press, adding that even her married daughter in Goma remains in hiding due to threats from FDLR operatives.

By March 2025, anti-Rwandan activists in Europe began circulating false claims that Mukamana, her seven children, and grandchild had been abducted in Goma by RDF and AFC/M23 forces. After months of rumors, Mukamana publicly refuted the allegations, confirming that she had voluntarily repatriated to Rwanda to rebuild her life in peace and security.

“I haven’t heard the sound of a gun for months - this is the first time in my life that I haven’t heard that sound,” Mukamana said. “There is peace here. My children are safe, they’ve gone back to school, and I no longer have a reason to hide.”

Her return is part of a larger wave of repatriations of Rwandans who had been living under FDLR influence in eastern Congo. Many have since returned home following the AFC/M23’s takeover of Goma, assisted by the United Nations High Commissioner for Refugees (UNHCR).

These returnees are initially hosted in temporary reception centers such as Nkamira in Rubavu District and Nyarushishi in Rusizi District, before being reintegrated into normal community life.

Mukamana’s story highlights a growing shift among former refugees and families of ex-combatants seeking stability back home - a move that signals renewed confidence in Rwanda’s peace and security.

title: DRC Forces Launch Major Strikes on AFC/M23-Held Areas in North Kivu
excerpt: The Democratic Republic of Congo (DRC) army has launched a series of major attacks on territories controlled by the AFC/M23 coalition in North Kivu province, the rebel group said on October 28, 2025.
title_en: DRC Forces Launch Major Strikes on AFC/M23-Held Areas in North Kivu
excerpt_en: The Democratic Republic of Congo (DRC) army has launched a series of major attacks on territories controlled by the AFC/M23 coalition in North Kivu province, the rebel group said on October 28, 2025.
body_en:
The Democratic Republic of Congo (DRC) army has launched a series of major attacks on territories controlled by the AFC/M23 coalition in North Kivu province, the rebel group said on October 28, 2025.

AFC/M23 spokesman Lawrence Kanyuka reported that the assaults began around 9:00 a.m., targeting locations including Kibati in Walikale, Bibwe, Nyabiondo, Bukombo in Masisi, and surrounding border areas. The attacks reportedly involved drones and long-range artillery.

“As a result of this indiscriminate provocation, children and women are being killed, and the number of injured and displaced is increasing at an alarming rate. By obstructing all peace steps taken by the international community, Kinshasa has made its intention clear: to wage war on the Congolese,” Kanyuka said.

The rebel spokesman emphasized that AFC/M23 would exercise its right to self-defense.

“Due to this murderous plan, the AFC/M23 has no other choice but to exercise its right to self-defense. We will use all possible means to protect civilians and destroy the criminals,” he added.

Meanwhile, the DRC army maintains that its operations are retaliatory. Army spokesman Maj. Gen. Sylvain Ekenge Bomusa told journalists that the strikes are a response to ongoing provocations.

“In the Church, they tell you that if someone slaps you on the left cheek, you will also slap the right cheek. We have not continued to watch the attacks all the time and with provocation,” he said.

The strikes come as the DRC government and AFC/M23 continue peace talks in Qatar, aimed at reaching a lasting resolution to the conflict. However, Benjamin Mbonimpa, Permanent Secretary of AFC/M23, warned that the renewed violence could disrupt the ongoing negotiations.

The conflict in eastern DRC has long been marked by cycles of armed clashes, civilian displacement, and humanitarian concerns, with international mediators closely monitoring the situation.

title: Rwandan Security Forces Commended Upon Return from Mozambique Peacekeeping Mission
excerpt: KIGALI - The Chief of Defence Staff, Maj Gen Alex Kagame, and Rwanda National Police Deputy Inspector General for Operations (DIGP) Vincent Sano, officially received a team of Rwandan soldiers and police officers…
title_en: Rwandan Security Forces Commended Upon Return from Mozambique Peacekeeping Mission
excerpt_en: KIGALI - The Chief of Defence Staff, Maj Gen Alex Kagame, and Rwanda National Police Deputy Inspector General for Operations (DIGP) Vincent Sano, officially received a team of Rwandan soldiers and police officers…
body_en:
KIGALI - The Chief of Defence Staff, Maj Gen Alex Kagame, and Rwanda National Police Deputy Inspector General for Operations (DIGP) Vincent Sano, officially received a team of Rwandan soldiers and police officers returning from a year-long peacekeeping mission in Cabo Delgado Province, Mozambique. The contingent, led by Major General Emmy K. Ruvusha, arrived in Kigali on Monday, October 27, 2025.

Maj Gen Kagame praised the personnel for their dedication and professionalism, urging them to continue upholding the values of the Rwandan security forces.

Rwandan troops and police have been deployed in Mozambique since 2021 to help combat the insurgency that has devastated the northern Cabo Delgado Province. Their efforts have reportedly helped drive out terrorists, restore security in affected areas, and enable displaced residents to return home.

In August 2025, Rwanda and Mozambique signed new agreements on security and trade cooperation, reinforcing bilateral collaboration in the region.

The returning personnel were replaced by a new team led by Maj Gen Vincent Gatama, which will continue to participate in counter-terrorism operations in Cabo Delgado.

This deployment highlights Rwanda’s ongoing commitment to regional peacekeeping and security efforts in East Africa.

title: DCG Urges Police to Promote Rwandans’ Welfare During Nationwide Tree-Planting Campaign
excerpt: GASABO, Rwanda - The Deputy Inspector General of Police (DIGP) for Administration and Personnel, DCG Jeanne Chantal Ujeneza, has reminded police officers that enhancing the welfare of Rwandans is a core part of their…
title_en: DCG Urges Police to Promote Rwandans’ Welfare During Nationwide Tree-Planting Campaign
excerpt_en: GASABO, Rwanda - The Deputy Inspector General of Police (DIGP) for Administration and Personnel, DCG Jeanne Chantal Ujeneza, has reminded police officers that enhancing the welfare of Rwandans is a core part of their…
body_en:
GASABO, Rwanda - The Deputy Inspector General of Police (DIGP) for Administration and Personnel, DCG Jeanne Chantal Ujeneza, has reminded police officers that enhancing the welfare of Rwandans is a core part of their responsibilities. She made the remarks on Saturday, October 25, during a community service event in Ndera Sector, Gasabo District, where police joined other security agencies, local authorities, and residents in a tree-planting exercise.

The activity took place on Ubwiza bwa Gasogi hill, a site known for its vulnerability to landslides. Participants planted 20,859 trees and dug additional holes for more trees to be planted in the coming days. The initiative, themed “My Tree, My Heritage,” is part of a nationwide campaign expected to run for three months to combat erosion and preserve the environment.

Speaking to participants, DIGP Ujeneza emphasized that the Rwanda National Police (RNP) is tasked not only with protecting lives and property but also with promoting community welfare and supporting national development. “Gathering here for a tree-planting event highlights the importance of trees in providing fresh air and maintaining a clean, beautiful Rwanda,” she said.

She added that the planted trees must be cared for to ensure their growth and long-term benefits, encouraging local residents to take ownership of their protection. “When you plant trees, you leave a legacy for future generations,” DIGP Ujeneza said, linking environmental stewardship to cultural preservation.

The DIGP also urged participants to collaborate with security agencies in preventing crime by reporting suspicious activities and acting as vigilant community members. She encouraged youth to focus on education, work, and personal development, while avoiding violence, drugs, and domestic conflicts that could hinder their opportunities.

The nationwide tree-planting campaign began on September 12 and will officially conclude on December 31, 2025, forming part of the government’s broader strategy to protect the environment and enhance community development.

title: Rwandan soldiers in South Sudan receive UN commendation medals
excerpt: JUBA, South Sudan - Rwandan troops deployed in the United Nations Mission in South Sudan (UNMISS) have been awarded medals of commendation for their exceptional service.
title_en: Rwandan soldiers in South Sudan receive UN commendation medals
excerpt_en: JUBA, South Sudan - Rwandan troops deployed in the United Nations Mission in South Sudan (UNMISS) have been awarded medals of commendation for their exceptional service.
body_en:
JUBA, South Sudan - Rwandan troops deployed in the United Nations Mission in South Sudan (UNMISS) have been awarded medals of commendation for their exceptional service. The ceremony took place at the Durupi military base on the outskirts of Juba, recognizing the contributions of RWANBATT-3 and RAU-13 contingents.

In his address, UN Force Commander Lt. Gen. Mohan Subramanian praised the Rwandan soldiers for their professionalism, dedication, and exemplary performance during peacekeeping operations. He highlighted Rwanda as one of the world’s top five troop-contributing countries.

Lt. Gen. Subramanian emphasized that the Rwandan troops’ conduct and commitment have significantly advanced peace and stability in South Sudan during their one-year deployment.

Col. Leodomir Uwizeyimana, Commander of the Rwanda Defence Forces in South Sudan, expressed gratitude to partner countries, local communities, and the people of South Sudan for their collaboration, which enabled the Rwandan forces to carry out their mission effectively.

He further commended the Rwandan troops for their discipline and dedication, reaffirming that they will continue to protect civilians and their property in line with the United Nations Charter.

The award underscores Rwanda’s growing reputation for professionalism and reliability in international peacekeeping operations.
